docs.title: Recognition signals — aap fast and slow pointers dekh rahe ho jab problem bole
docs.text:
• "cycle", "loop", "does it repeat" — linked list mein, ya kisi bhi sequence mein jahan har state se exactly ek next state jaata hai.
  • "middle of the linked list" — ek hi pass mein middle chahiye, length pehle count kiye bina.
  • "nth node from the end" — yeh gap wala variant hai (dono same speed, lekin ek n aage se start).
  • "find the duplicate number" jahan array ko implicitly ek function i -> arr[i] samjha ja sakta hai.
  • "happy number" type problems — number pe repeatedly ek operation lagao aur dekho cycle mein phansta hai ya nahi.
  • Constraint bole "O(1) extra space" aur aapka natural solution ek set use kar raha ho — yeh sabse bada hint hai. Set wala solution O(n) space leta hai; fast/slow O(1) mein wahi kaam karta hai.
  • Linked list ho aur aapko do jagah ek saath chahiye ho (middle aur end, ya cycle start aur head).

docs.title: Yeh pattern kaam kyun karta hai — asli intuition
docs.text:
Do runners ek circular track par hain. Ek 1 metre per second, dusra 2 metre per second. Agar track circular hai toh tez wala dheere wale ko zaroor pakdega — kyunki har second unke beech ka gap exactly 1 metre kam hota hai. Gap kabhi skip nahi hota, isliye woh exactly 0 par aayega, matlab dono ek hi node par honge.

Agar track sidha hai (koi cycle nahi), toh tez wala pehle end par pahunch jaayega aur None mil jaayega.

Yeh "gap har step par exactly 1 kam hota hai" wala argument hi poore pattern ka proof hai. Isko interview mein bolna chahiye — yeh dikhata hai ki aapne ratta nahi maara.

Important: speeds 1 aur 2 hi kyun? Kyunki gap exactly 1 se ghatta hai, toh gap kabhi "jump over" nahi karta. Agar speeds 1 aur 3 hote toh gap 2 se ghatta, aur cycle length even/odd ke hisaab se dono cross kar sakte hain bina mile — technically phir bhi modular arithmetic se milte hain, lekin proof zyada complicated ho jaata hai. 1 aur 2 sabse simple aur hamesha correct.

docs.title: Template code
docs.text:
class ListNode:
    """Interview mein yeh class aksar diya hua hota hai, lekin khud likh sako toh accha."""
    def __init__(self, val=0, nxt=None):
        self.val = val                    # node ka data
        self.next = nxt                   # agla node ka reference, ya None


def has_cycle(head):
    """Template A: cycle hai ya nahi."""
    slow = fast = head                    # dono head se start
    while fast and fast.next:             # fast ko do steps chahiye, dono exist karne chahiye
        slow = slow.next                  # ek step
        fast = fast.next.next             # do step
        if slow is fast:                  # mil gaye -> cycle
            return True
    return False                          # fast None par pahunch gaya -> koi cycle nahi


def find_middle(head):
    """Template B: middle node (even length par second middle)."""
    slow = fast = head
    while fast and fast.next:
        slow = slow.next
        fast = fast.next.next
    return slow                           # fast end par, slow exactly aadhe raste par

Template ka core idea: fast hamesha slow se double distance cover karta hai. Toh jab fast n par ho, slow n/2 par hoga — yeh middle deta hai. Aur agar raasta circular ho toh double speed wala wrap around karke slow ko peeche se pakad leta hai — yeh cycle deta hai. Ek hi mechanism, do alag use.

docs.title: Problem 3.1 — Linked List Cycle Detection
docs.text:
Problem statement

Ek linked list ka head diya hai. Bataao ki isme cycle hai ya nahi. Cycle ka matlab: koi node ka next list mein peeche kisi node ko point kar raha hai, toh traversal kabhi khatam nahi hoga.

Example 1:  3 -> 2 -> 0 -> -4
                 ^          |
                 |__________|
Output: True

Example 2:  1 -> 2 -> None
Output: False

Pehla instinct — brute force

Har visited node ko ek set mein daal do. Agar koi node dobara mila toh cycle hai.

def has_cycle_brute(head):
    seen = set()                          # 1: visited nodes ke object ids
    current = head                        # 2: traversal pointer
    while current:                        # 3: jab tak list khatam na ho
        if current in seen:               # 4: pehle dekha tha? -> cycle
            return True                   # 5
        seen.add(current)                 # 6: mark visited
        current = current.next            # 7: aage badho
    return False                          # 8: None mil gaya -> koi cycle nahi

Line by line — kyun aise likha hai

  1. seen = set() — set kyun, list kyun nahi? Kyunki current in seen set par O(1) hai aur list par O(n). List use karte toh poora solution O(n^2) ho jaata.
  2. current = head — head ko directly modify nahi karte kyunki caller ko head chahiye ho sakta hai (yahan matter nahi karta lekin habit acchi hai).
  3. while current: — None falsy hai, toh yeh "jab tak node exist kare" ka short form hai.
  4. if current in seen — yahan node object compare ho raha hai, node ki value nahi. Yeh critical hai: [1, 2, 1] mein do nodes ki value 1 hai lekin woh alag objects hain. Python ka default in for objects identity/equality par chalta hai, aur ListNode mein __eq__ define nahi kiya toh identity use hoti hai — exactly jo chahiye.
  5. return True.
  6. seen.add(current) — check ke baad add karte hain, pehle nahi. Agar pehle add karte toh line 4 hamesha immediately True de deti.
  7. current = current.next.
  8. return False.

Complexity: Time O(n), Space O(n) — yehi problem hai.

Isme problem kya hai

Space O(n). Ek million node ki list par yeh ek million object references store karega. Interviewer almost hamesha bolta hai "can you do it in O(1) space?" — aur agar aap nahi kar paye toh yeh question fail hai.

The insight

Cycle ek circular track hai. Do runners alag speed se daudao. Agar track circular hai, tez wala dheere wale ko lap kar dega aur exactly usi node par milega — kyunki cycle ke andar unke beech ka gap har step par exactly 1 kam hota hai, aur 1 se ghatne wali cheez 0 ko skip nahi kar sakti. Agar track sidha hai, tez wala pehle None tak pahunch jaayega. Isliye "mile ya None mila" — yehi poora answer hai, aur ismein koi memory nahi chahiye.

Optimal solution

def has_cycle(head):
    slow = head                           # 1: dheere wala pointer, 1 step per iteration
    fast = head                           # 2: tez wala pointer, 2 steps per iteration
    while fast is not None and fast.next is not None:   # 3: fast do step le sakta hai?
        slow = slow.next                  # 4: slow ek aage
        fast = fast.next.next             # 5: fast do aage
        if slow is fast:                  # 6: same object par? -> cycle
            return True                   # 7
    return False                          # 8: loop toota matlab fast list ke end par pahuncha

Line by line — kyun aise likha hai

  1. slow = head — dono ek hi jagah se start hote hain. Alag jagah se start karna bhi kaam karta hai lekin "meeting" ka proof gadbada jaata hai, isliye standard yehi hai.
  2. fast = head.
  3. while fast is not None and fast.next is not None: — yeh line poore solution ki sabse nazuk line hai. Do checks hain kyunki line 5 mein fast.next.next likhna hai:
  4. agar fast None hai toh fast.next AttributeError dega,
  5. agar fast.next None hai toh fast.next.next AttributeError dega. Python ka and short-circuit karta hai, toh pehla check fail hone par dusra evaluate hi nahi hoga — isliye order ulta nahi kar sakte. while fast.next and fast: likhna crash karega.
  6. slow = slow.next — slow ke liye null check ki zaroorat nahi kyunki slow hamesha fast se peeche hai; agar fast valid hai toh slow bhi valid hai.
  7. fast = fast.next.next — dono steps ek saath. Agar aap fast = fast.next do baar likhte toh beech mein null check karna padta.
  8. if slow is fast: — is use kiya, == nahi. is identity check hai (same object in memory). == values compare karta agar __eq__ defined ho. Cycle detection object identity ka sawaal hai, value ka nahi. Habit ke liye hamesha is likho.
  9. return True.
  10. return False — loop se bahar aane ka matlab fast ya fast.next None ho gaya, matlab list ka genuine end mila, matlab cycle nahi.

Check line 6 ka placement. Move ke baad check karte hain, pehle nahi. Agar loop ke shuru mein check karte toh pehli iteration mein hi slow is fast True hota (dono head par hain) aur galat True return hota.

Dry run — cycle wali list: 3 -> 2 -> 0 -> -4 -> (back to 2)

Nodes ko A(3), B(2), C(0), D(-4) naam de dete hain. D.next = B.

Iteration slow (start) fast (start) fast valid? slow (after) fast (after) slow is fast? init A A — — — — 1 A A Yes (A, B exist) B C No 2 B C Yes (C, D exist) C B (D.next=B) No 3 C B Yes (B, C exist) D D Yes → True

Iteration 2 dekho — fast C -> D -> B gaya, matlab wrap ho gaya. Iteration 3 mein dono D par mile.

Dry run — no cycle: 1 -> 2 -> None. Nodes P(1), Q(2).

Iteration slow fast fast and fast.next? Action init P P — — 1 P P Yes (P, Q exist) slow=Q, fast=Q.next.next → None 2 Q None fast is None → loop exit return False

Complexity

  • Time: O(n). No-cycle case mein fast n/2 iterations mein end tak pahunch jaata hai. Cycle case mein: slow ko cycle mein ghusne ke liye at most n steps lagte hain, aur uske baad gap har step 1 kam hota hai, toh at most cycle-length steps aur. Total O(n).
  • Space: O(1). Sirf do pointers, input size se independent.

Edge cases

Case Input Output Kyun Empty list head = None False Line 3 ka pehla check turant fail Single node, no cycle A -> None False fast.next None hai Single node, self loop A -> A True Iteration 1: slow=A, fast=A → mile Two nodes, cycle A -> B -> A True Iteration 1: slow=B, fast=A; iteration 2: slow=A, fast=B; iteration 3: mile Long tail, small cycle 1000 nodes then 2-cycle True Slow ko tail cross karne mein time lagta hai, phir jaldi milte hain Whole list is one cycle A->B->C->A True

Variations

  • Cycle ka start node lautao — Problem 3.2, Floyd ka phase 2.
  • Cycle ki length lautao — meeting point se ek pointer chalao aur wapas usi point par aane tak steps count karo.
  • Cycle ko remove karo — cycle start ke ek node pehle wale ka next None kar do.
  • Doubly linked list mein cycle — same algorithm, next hi use hota hai.
  • Do lists intersect karti hain ya nahi — alag problem, lekin same "two pointer on lists" family.

Interview answer: "The naive approach is to keep a set of visited node objects and walk the list — if I ever see the same node twice, there's a cycle. That's O(n) time but also O(n) space.

To get O(1) space I use Floyd's cycle detection, the tortoise and hare. Two pointers start at the head. Slow moves one node per step, fast moves two.

The reason this works is worth stating: if there's a cycle, both pointers eventually end up inside it, and once they're both inside, the gap between them shrinks by exactly one every step. A quantity that decreases by exactly one can't skip past zero, so they must land on the same node. If there's no cycle, fast reaches the end first and I return false.

Two implementation details matter. The loop condition checks both fast and fast.next, in that order, because I dereference fast.next.next inside — and Python's and short-circuits so the order protects me. And I compare with is, not ==, because this is a question about object identity, not values — two different nodes can hold the same value.

O(n) time, O(1) space."

docs.title: Problem 3.2 — Find The Start Of The Cycle
docs.text:
Problem statement

Cycle hai — ab woh node lautao jahan se cycle shuru hoti hai. Agar cycle nahi hai toh None.

3 -> 2 -> 0 -> -4
     ^          |
     |__________|
Output: node with value 2

Pehla instinct — brute force

Set wala solution yahan actually seedha answer de deta hai: pehla node jo dobara mila, wahi cycle ka start hai.

def cycle_start_brute(head):
    seen = set()                          # 1: visited nodes
    current = head                        # 2
    while current:                        # 3
        if current in seen:               # 4: dobara mila
            return current                # 5: yehi cycle ka entry point hai
        seen.add(current)                 # 6
        current = current.next            # 7
    return None                           # 8: cycle nahi

Line by line — kyun aise likha hai

1-3. Same as 3.1. 4-5. current in seen — pehla repeat hamesha cycle ka start hota hai. Kyun? Kyunki tail ke nodes exactly ek baar visit hote hain (unke andar koi aata nahi), aur cycle ka entry node hi woh pehla node hai jise do raaste se pahuncha ja sakta hai — ek tail se, ek cycle ke andar se. Toh traversal mein woh sabse pehle repeat hoga. 6-8. Same as 3.1.

Complexity: Time O(n), Space O(n).

Isme problem kya hai

Phir wahi — O(n) space. Aur interviewer specifically O(1) maangega, kyunki yeh problem hi Floyd's algorithm ka phase 2 sikhane ke liye poochi jaati hai.

The insight

Yeh document ka sabse "magic-looking" result hai, isliye main iska proof poora likhta hoon — kyunki bina proof ke yeh bas ek yaad kiya hua trick hai, aur interviewer poochega "why does that work?"

Naam de dete hain: - F = head se cycle ke start tak ki distance (tail ki length). - C = cycle ki length. - a = cycle ke start se meeting point tak ki distance (cycle ke andar, aage ki direction mein).

Jab dono milte hain: - slow ne total chala: F + a steps. (Slow cycle mein ek baar se zyada nahi ghoomta — proof: slow cycle mein ghusne ke waqt fast pehle se cycle mein hai, aur gap at most C-1 hai, aur gap har step 1 kam hota hai, toh at most C-1 steps mein mil jaate hain, jo ek poore lap se kam hai.) - fast ne total chala: 2(F + a) steps, kyunki double speed. - Fast ne slow se jitna zyada chala, woh cycle ke poore laps hone chahiye: 2(F + a) - (F + a) = F + a = nC kisi integer n >= 1 ke liye.

Toh F + a = nC, matlab F = nC - a.

Ab isko padho: head se F steps chalna aur meeting point se nC - a steps chalna — dono same jagah pahunchate hain. Kyunki meeting point cycle ke start se a aage hai, toh wahan se nC - a chalne ka matlab hai n poore laps minus a, jo exactly cycle ke start par le aata hai.

Toh algorithm: ek pointer head par rakho, ek meeting point par. Dono ko 1-1 step chalao. Jahan milenge wahi cycle ka start hai.

Optimal solution

def cycle_start(head):
    slow = fast = head                    # 1: phase 1 -- meeting point dhoondo
    meeting = None                        # 2: mila toh yahan store karenge
    while fast and fast.next:             # 3: standard safe condition
        slow = slow.next                  # 4
        fast = fast.next.next             # 5
        if slow is fast:                  # 6: cycle confirm
            meeting = slow                # 7: meeting node yaad rakho
            break                         # 8: phase 1 khatam
    if meeting is None:                   # 9: loop natural end -> koi cycle nahi
        return None                       # 10
    p1 = head                             # 11: phase 2 -- ek pointer head se
    p2 = meeting                          # 12: dusra meeting point se
    while p1 is not p2:                   # 13: dono ab SAME speed par
        p1 = p1.next                      # 14
        p2 = p2.next                      # 15
    return p1                             # 16: yeh cycle ka start hai

Line by line — kyun aise likha hai

  1. slow = fast = head — Python mein yeh dono ko same object bind karta hai; kyunki hum reassign karte hain (mutate nahi), koi aliasing bug nahi.
  2. meeting = None — sentinel. Iski zaroorat hai kyunki loop do tarah se khatam ho sakta hai (cycle mila, ya list khatam), aur dono ko distinguish karna hai.
  3. while fast and fast.next — 3.1 wali hi safety. 4-5. Standard 1-step / 2-step. 6-8. Mile toh node save karke break. break zaroori hai warna agli iteration mein woh aage badh jaayenge aur meeting point kho jaayega. 9-10. meeting is None — matlab loop fast ke None hone se toota, cycle nahi thi. if not meeting bhi likh sakte the lekin is None explicit hai (aur agar kabhi node ka __bool__ False hota toh yeh bug se bachaata).
  4. p1 = head — head se, slow se nahi. Formula F = nC - a head se distance ke baare mein hai.
  5. p2 = meeting.
  6. while p1 is not p2: — ab dono ki speed same hai (1 step). Yeh sabse common galti hai — log phase 2 mein bhi fast ko 2 steps chalate hain, jo galat answer deta hai. Formula tabhi kaam karta hai jab dono equal steps chalein. 14-15. Dono ek ek step.
  7. return p1 — p2 return karna bhi wahi hai, dono ek hi node hain.

Edge case jo line 13 automatically handle karti hai: agar cycle ka start head hi hai (F = 0), toh p1 aur p2 ka comparison pehli hi baar True ho sakta hai — kyunki F = 0 ka matlab nC = a, aur a < C hone se n must be such that meeting point exactly head par hai. Loop body chalti hi nahi, head return ho jaata hai. Sahi.

Dry run — list: 1 -> 2 -> 3 -> 4 -> 5 -> (back to 3)

Nodes: A(1), B(2), C(3), D(4), E(5). E.next = C. Yahan F = 2 (A→B→C), C_len = 3 (C,D,E).

Phase 1:

Iteration slow before fast before slow after fast after Met? 1 A A B C No 2 B C C E No 3 C E D D Yes → meeting = D

Check formula: a = C se D tak = 1. F + a = 2 + 1 = 3 = 1 × C_len = 3. Correct.

Phase 2:

Step p1 p2 p1 is p2? Action init A D No move 1 B E No move 2 C C Yes return C

C node value 3 — sahi, cycle wahin se shuru hoti hai.

Complexity

  • Time: O(n). Phase 1 O(n), phase 2 at most F + C steps jo O(n) hai. Do linear passes = O(n).
  • Space: O(1). Teen pointers.

Edge cases

Case Input Output Kyun No cycle 1->2->None None meeting None reh jaata hai Empty None None Loop chalta hi nahi Self loop at head A->A A Meeting A par, phase 2 turant match Cycle starts at head A->B->C->A A F = 0, phase 2 zero steps Cycle is last node only A->B->B B C_len = 1 Long tail 10^5 tail + 3-cycle cycle start Phase 2 poore tail par chalta hai

Variations

  • Cycle ki length — meeting point se chalo aur wapas meeting point par aane tak count karo.
  • Cycle ko todo — cycle start se ek node pehle wale ka next = None.
  • Kitne nodes cycle ke bahar hain — phase 2 ke steps count karo, wahi F hai.
  • Find the Duplicate Number (LeetCode 287) — bilkul yehi algorithm, array ko function ki tarah treat karke. Problem 3.6 dekho.

Interview answer: "Phase one is the standard tortoise and hare — I find a node where slow and fast meet, which proves a cycle exists and gives me one node inside it.

Phase two is where the actual result comes from. Let F be the distance from the head to the cycle entry, C the cycle length, and a the distance from the entry to the meeting point. When they meet, slow has walked F plus a, and fast has walked exactly twice that. The difference — which is also F plus a — has to be a whole number of laps, so F plus a equals n times C. Rearranged, F equals n·C minus a.

That equation says something concrete: walking F steps from the head lands in the same place as walking n·C minus a steps from the meeting point. So I put one pointer at the head and one at the meeting point, move both one step at a time, and where they collide is the cycle entry.

The mistake I'd call out is keeping the fast pointer at double speed in phase two. The derivation depends on both pointers moving at the same rate, so that breaks it.

O(n) time, O(1) space."

docs.title: Problem 3.3 — Middle Of The Linked List
docs.text:
Problem statement

Linked list ka middle node lautao. Agar do middle hain (even length), toh dusra middle lautao.

Input:  1 -> 2 -> 3 -> 4 -> 5          Output: node 3
Input:  1 -> 2 -> 3 -> 4 -> 5 -> 6     Output: node 4   (dusra middle)

Pehla instinct — brute force

Pehle poori list count karo, phir n // 2 steps chalo.

def middle_brute(head):
    n = 0                                 # 1: length counter
    current = head                        # 2: pehla pass ka pointer
    while current:                        # 3: poori list ginno
        n += 1                            # 4
        current = current.next            # 5
    current = head                        # 6: dobara shuru se
    for _ in range(n // 2):               # 7: n//2 steps aage
        current = current.next            # 8
    return current                        # 9: yeh middle hai

Line by line — kyun aise likha hai

  1. n = 0 — length rakhne ke liye. 2-5. Pehla pass: sirf ginti. current ko head se alag variable rakha kyunki head ko phir se chahiye.
  2. current = head — reset. Yahi wajah hai ki head ko step 2 mein overwrite nahi kiya.
  3. for _ in range(n // 2) — n // 2 kyun, (n-1) // 2 kyun nahi? Length 5 par 5 // 2 = 2 steps → index 2 → node 3. Sahi. Length 6 par 6 // 2 = 3 → index 3 → node 4, yaani dusra middle. Problem exactly yehi maang rahi hai. Agar pehla middle chahiye hota toh (n - 1) // 2 likhte.
  4. current = current.next.
  5. return current.

Complexity: Time O(n) but do passes, Space O(1).

Isme problem kya hai

Space toh theek hai, lekin do passes hain. Interview mein sawaal aksar aise aata hai: "can you do it in one pass?" — aur asli baat yeh hai ki agar list ek stream ho (jise aap dobara traverse nahi kar sakte, jaise ek file jo ek baar padhi ja sakti hai), toh do-pass solution possible hi nahi hai.

The insight

Agar ek pointer double speed se chale, toh jab tez wala end par pahunchega, dheere wala exactly aadhe raste par hoga. Yeh definition hi middle ki hai. Kisi counting ki zaroorat nahi — end ka pata chalna hi middle ka pata chal jaana hai.

Optimal solution

def middle_node(head):
    slow = head                           # 1: yeh middle par rukega
    fast = head                           # 2: yeh end tak jaayega
    while fast is not None and fast.next is not None:  # 3: fast ke liye do steps bache hain?
        slow = slow.next                  # 4: ek step
        fast = fast.next.next             # 5: do step
    return slow                           # 6: fast end par -> slow middle par

Line by line — kyun aise likha hai

1-2. Dono head se. Dono ka same start hona zaroori hai, warna "aadha" ka relation toot jaata hai. 3. while fast is not None and fast.next is not None: — yeh condition hi decide karti hai ki even length par kaunsa middle milega. - Odd length (5): fast A→C→E, phir E.next None → loop ruka. slow do steps chala → C (index 2). Sahi. - Even length (6): fast A→C→E, phir E.next = F exist karta hai toh ek aur iteration → fast F.next.next... wait, fast = E, E.next = F, F exists toh loop chalta hai, fast = E.next.next = F.next = None, slow teen steps chala → D (index 3), yaani dusra middle. - Agar pehla middle chahiye toh condition badal do: while fast.next is not None and fast.next.next is not None: — tab fast hamesha ek node pehle ruk jaata hai aur slow ek kam chalta hai. 4-5. Standard. 6. return slow.

Ek chhoti si baat jo interviewer test karta hai: yeh solution head = None par crash nahi karta — line 3 ka pehla check None is not None False deta hai, loop skip, None return. Aur bahut se log yahan while fast.next and fast.next.next likh dete hain jo head = None par crash karta hai. Isliye main pehle fast check karta hoon.

Dry run — 1 -> 2 -> 3 -> 4 -> 5 (nodes A,B,C,D,E)

Iteration slow before fast before fast and fast.next? slow after fast after init A A — — — 1 A A Yes (A, B) B C 2 B C Yes (C, D) C E 3 C E E.next is None → stop C E return — — — C (value 3) —

Dry run — 1 -> 2 -> 3 -> 4 -> 5 -> 6 (A..F)

Iteration slow before fast before Condition slow after fast after 1 A A Yes B C 2 B C Yes C E 3 C E Yes (E.next = F) D F.next = None 4 D None fast is None → stop D None return — — — D (value 4) —

Dusra middle mila, jaisa maanga tha.

Complexity

  • Time: O(n). Fast n/2 iterations chalta hai, har iteration O(1). Ek hi pass.
  • Space: O(1).

Edge cases

Case Input Output Kyun Empty None None Line 3 pehla check Single A A A.next None, loop skip Two nodes A->B B Ek iteration, slow=B Three nodes A->B->C B Ek iteration Four nodes A->B->C->D C Do iterations List with cycle — Infinite loop Yeh function cycle assume nahi karta — clarify karo

Variations

  • Pehla middle chahiye — condition while fast.next and fast.next.next.
  • Middle delete karo (LeetCode 2095) — middle se ek pehle wala node bhi track karo (prev).
  • Nth node from end — do pointers same speed, dusra n aage se start.
  • List ko do halves mein todo — slow par cut karke prev.next = None.
  • Palindrome check — Problem 3.5, middle nikaal kar second half reverse.

Interview answer: "The obvious approach counts the length first, then walks half of it. That's two passes, and it wouldn't work at all if this were a stream I can only read once.

One pass: two pointers from the head, one moving one node at a time and one moving two. Fast covers exactly twice the distance slow does, so the moment fast reaches the end, slow is at the halfway point. That's the definition of the middle — I never need the length.

The loop condition is doing the real work. Checking both fast and fast.next means for an even-length list I take one extra iteration and land on the second middle, which is what the problem asked for. If they wanted the first middle I'd shift the condition to fast.next and fast.next.next instead.

I also check fast before fast.next so an empty list returns None rather than crashing.

O(n) time, O(1) space, single pass."

docs.title: Problem 3.4 — Happy Number
docs.text:
Problem statement

Ek number n liya. Repeatedly usko uske digits ke squares ke sum se replace karo. Agar process 1 par pahunch jaaye toh number "happy" hai. Agar loop mein phas jaaye toh happy nahi.

Input: 19
19 -> 1^2 + 9^2 = 82
82 -> 8^2 + 2^2 = 68
68 -> 6^2 + 8^2 = 100
100 -> 1 + 0 + 0 = 1     -> happy
Output: True

Input: 2
2 -> 4 -> 16 -> 37 -> 58 -> 89 -> 145 -> 42 -> 20 -> 4 (repeat!)
Output: False

Pehla instinct — brute force

Har dekha hua number ek set mein daalo. Agar 1 mila → True. Agar koi number dobara mila → cycle → False.

def is_happy_brute(n):
    seen = set()                          # 1: ab tak dekhe gaye numbers
    while n != 1 and n not in seen:       # 2: na 1 mila, na repeat mila
        seen.add(n)                       # 3: current ko mark karo
        n = sum_of_squares(n)             # 4: agla number
    return n == 1                         # 5: loop kis wajah se toota?


def sum_of_squares(num):
    total = 0                             # 6: accumulator
    while num > 0:                        # 7: digits khatam hone tak
        num, digit = divmod(num, 10)      # 8: last digit nikaalo aur num chhota karo
        total += digit * digit            # 9: square add karo
    return total                          # 10

Line by line — kyun aise likha hai

  1. seen = set() — O(1) membership ke liye.
  2. while n != 1 and n not in seen: — do exit conditions ek saath. Order matter karta hai stylistically nahi lekin readability ke liye "success condition pehle" acha lagta hai.
  3. seen.add(n) — check ke baad add, warna line 2 pehli iteration mein hi toot jaata.
  4. n = sum_of_squares(n) — transition function.
  5. return n == 1 — yeh line clever hai. Loop do wajah se toot sakta hai; agar n == 1 ki wajah se toota toh happy, agar repeat ki wajah se toota toh n != 1 hoga. Ek hi expression dono cases handle kar leta hai — alag flags rakhne ki zaroorat nahi.
  6. total = 0.
  7. while num > 0: — 0 par ruk jaata hai. Note: n positive hai, isliye >= 0 galat hota (infinite loop).
  8. num, digit = divmod(num, 10) — divmod ek call mein quotient aur remainder deta hai. Alternative digit = num % 10; num //= 10 — bilkul same, bas do lines.
  9. total += digit * digit — digit ** 2 bhi chalega lekin digit * digit micro-faster hai aur zyada explicit.
  10. return total.

Complexity: Time O(log n) per step (digits ki count), aur steps kitne? Practically chhote — kyunki koi bhi number jaldi hi 3-digit range se neeche aa jaata hai (sabse bada 3-digit sum 999 → 243). Space O(k) jahan k cycle tak dekhe gaye numbers.

Isme problem kya hai

Space. Set chahiye. Aur yeh problem specifically isliye poochi jaati hai ki interviewer dekh sake ki aap "repeatedly apply a function" ko ek implicit linked list ke roop mein dekh paate ho ya nahi.

The insight

Yahan asli baat samajhna: n -> sum_of_squares(n) ek function hai, aur har number se exactly ek agla number nikalta hai. Yeh bilkul linked list ka structure hai — har node ka exactly ek next.

Aur sequence bounded hai (numbers arbitrarily bade nahi hote — 3 digits se upar wale hamesha neeche gir jaate hain), toh sequence ya toh 1 par ruk jaayegi ya zaroor repeat karegi. Yaani: ya toh 1, ya cycle.

Toh ab yeh Problem 3.1 hi hai — cycle detection — bas "node" ki jagah "number" hai aur node.next ki jagah sum_of_squares(number). Aur 1 ko special-case karne ki bhi zaroorat nahi: 1 khud ek self-loop hai (1 -> 1), toh cycle detect hone par bas check karo ki cycle 1 par hai ya kahin aur.

Optimal solution

def is_happy(n):
    def next_num(num):                    # 1: "node.next" ka equivalent
        total = 0                         # 2
        while num > 0:                    # 3
            num, d = divmod(num, 10)      # 4
            total += d * d                # 5
        return total                      # 6

    slow = n                              # 7: ek step wala
    fast = next_num(n)                    # 8: do step wala -- EK step aage se start
    while fast != 1 and slow != fast:     # 9: na 1 mila, na mile aapas mein
        slow = next_num(slow)             # 10: slow ek step
        fast = next_num(next_num(fast))   # 11: fast do step
    return fast == 1                      # 12: 1 mila toh happy

Line by line — kyun aise likha hai

1-6. next_num — nested function rakha kyunki yeh sirf yahin use hoti hai; module-level bhi bilkul theek hai. Line 4 mein divmod last digit aur baaki number dono deta hai. 7. slow = n — start. 8. fast = next_num(n) — yahan fast ko ek step aage se start kiya, dono ko n par nahi rakha. Kyun? Kyunki line 9 ka slow != fast loop ke shuru mein check hota hai. Agar dono n par hote toh pehli hi check slow == fast True de deti aur loop chalta hi nahi. Do options hain: - fast ko ek step aage start karo (yeh version), ya - do-while style likho: loop body pehle chalao, phir check karo. Python mein do-while nahi hai, isliye pehla option zyada saaf hai. 9. while fast != 1 and slow != fast: — do exit: 1 mil gaya (happy) ya dono mile (cycle jo 1 par nahi hai). slow != 1 check karne ki zaroorat nahi kyunki fast hamesha aage hai, toh 1 pehle fast ko milega. 10. slow = next_num(slow). 11. fast = next_num(next_num(fast)) — do baar apply karna hi "two steps" hai. Ek hi baar likhne se yeh algorithm nahi rahega. 12. return fast == 1 — slow check karna galat hoga: agar loop fast == 1 se toota toh slow abhi kahin peeche hai.

Ek sawaal jo aata hai: "loop terminate hone ki guarantee kya hai?" Jawab: 3-digit se bada koi bhi number ek step mein chhota ho jaata hai (999 → 243, aur 4-digit ka max 9999 → 324). Toh sequence hamesha 1 se 243 ke range mein aa jaati hai. Us finite range mein infinite sequence hai, toh pigeonhole principle se koi value repeat karegi — matlab cycle guaranteed hai (ya 1 mil jaayega).

Dry run — n = 19

Step slow fast fast == 1? slow == fast? Action init 19 82 No No enter loop 1 82 next(next(82)) = next(68) = 100 No No continue 2 68 next(next(100)) = next(1) = 1 Yes — exit loop return — 1 — — True

Step 1 detail: slow 19 -> 82. fast 82 -> 68 -> 100. Step 2 detail: slow 82 -> 68. fast 100 -> 1 -> 1 (kyunki next(1) = 1).

Dry run — n = 2. Sequence: 2, 4, 16, 37, 58, 89, 145, 42, 20, 4, 16, ...

Step slow fast fast == 1? slow == fast? init 2 4 No No 1 4 37 No No 2 16 58 No No 3 37 145 No No 4 58 20 No No 5 89 16 No No 6 145 37 No No 7 42 58 No No 8 20 145 No No 9 4 20 No No 10 16 4 No No 11 37 37 No Yes → exit return — 37 (!= 1) — False

Fast ke moves check karo step 1 par: 4 -> 16 -> 37. Sahi.

Complexity

  • Time: O(log n) first step ke liye (digits count), aur uske baad numbers 243 se chhote ho jaate hain toh steps constant-bounded hain. Practically O(log n) total.
  • Space: O(1). Do integers. Yeh brute force ke O(k) set se better hai.

Edge cases

Case Input Output Kyun n = 1 1 True fast = next(1) = 1, loop chalta hi nahi, return True n = 7 7 True 7→49→97→130→10→1 n = 2 2 False Upar wala cycle Very large 10^9 depends Pehla step 4-digit se neeche le aata hai n = 0 0 False next(0) = 0 (while loop chalta nahi), self-loop at 0. Constraint usually n >= 1 — clarify karo Repunit 1111111 True 7 ones → 7 → happy

Variations

  • Alag transition function — digits ka cube, ya digits ka sum. Same algorithm, next_num badal do.
  • Cycle ki length lautao — meeting point se ek loop chalao.
  • Sabhi happy numbers 1 se n tak — memoisation zyada useful ho jaata hai than Floyd.
  • Circular Array Loop (LeetCode 457) — array indices par same idea, plus direction constraint.
  • Set-based version defend karo — agar interviewer bole "why not just use a set", jawab: set O(k) space leta hai; Floyd O(1). Chhote inputs par set fine hai aur zyada readable — trade-off bolna acha lagta hai.

Interview answer: "The key observation is that this isn't really a number problem — it's a linked list problem in disguise. Each number maps to exactly one next number under the digit-square-sum function, which is the same structure as a node with one next pointer.

And the sequence is bounded: any number above three digits shrinks immediately, so everything falls into the range one to 243. A never-ending walk through a finite set has to repeat, so by pigeonhole the sequence either reaches 1 or enters a cycle. There's no third option.

So this is Floyd's cycle detection. Slow applies the function once per step, fast applies it twice. I stop when fast hits 1 — happy — or when the two meet, which means a cycle that isn't at 1.

One detail: I start fast one step ahead of slow rather than at the same value, because my loop checks the equality at the top. If they both started at n the loop body would never run.

This is O(1) space versus O(k) for the obvious set-based version. I'd mention that the set version is more readable and perfectly fine for small inputs — the O(1) version is what to reach for if space is constrained."

docs.title: Problem 3.5 — Palindrome Linked List
docs.text:
Problem statement

Singly linked list diya hai. Bataao ki values ka sequence palindrome hai ya nahi.

Input: 1 -> 2 -> 2 -> 1        Output: True
Input: 1 -> 2 -> 3 -> 2 -> 1   Output: True
Input: 1 -> 2                  Output: False

Constraint: O(n) time aur O(1) space.

Pehla instinct — brute force

Saari values ek list mein copy karo, phir reverse se compare karo.

def is_palindrome_brute(head):
    values = []                           # 1: values ko array mein nikaalo
    current = head                        # 2
    while current:                        # 3: poori list traverse
        values.append(current.val)        # 4: sirf value chahiye, node nahi
        current = current.next            # 5
    return values == values[::-1]         # 6: array ko apne reverse se compare

Line by line — kyun aise likha hai

  1. values = [] — Python list random access deti hai, linked list nahi. Yehi poora point hai. 2-5. Standard traversal, values copy.
  2. values == values[::-1] — [::-1] ek naya reversed list banata hai (O(n) time aur O(n) extra space). Alternative two-pointer compare bhi likh sakte the: 
    i, j = 0, len(values) - 1
while i < j:
    if values[i] != values[j]:
        return False
    i += 1
    j -= 1
return True
    Yeh extra copy bachaata hai lekin values khud abhi bhi O(n) hai, toh asymptotic space wahi hai.

Complexity: Time O(n), Space O(n).

Isme problem kya hai

O(n) space. Aur yeh problem hi isliye poochi jaati hai ki dekha ja sake ki aap teen alag techniques compose kar sakte ho ya nahi: middle dhoondhna (fast/slow), half reverse karna, aur do halves compare karna. Yeh "can you chain patterns" wala test hai.

The insight

Singly linked list mein peeche nahi ja sakte — yehi asli dikkat hai. Lekin agar second half ko reverse kar dein, toh ab do lists hain jo dono aage ki direction mein chalti hain: pehli half start se, doosri half (ab reversed) end se. Unhe side by side compare karo — yeh exactly palindrome check hai.

Aur "second half kahan se shuru hoti hai" — woh fast/slow se ek pass mein mil jaata hai. Toh: middle dhoondo → second half reverse karo → compare karo → (optional) list restore karo.

Optimal solution

def is_palindrome(head):
    if head is None or head.next is None:  # 1: 0 ya 1 node hamesha palindrome
        return True                        # 2

    slow = fast = head                     # 3: STEP A -- middle dhoondo
    while fast.next and fast.next.next:    # 4: PEHLA middle par rukna hai is baar
        slow = slow.next                   # 5
        fast = fast.next.next              # 6
    # ab slow = pehli half ka aakhri node

    second = reverse_list(slow.next)       # 7: STEP B -- second half reverse
    slow.next = None                       # 8: dono halves ko alag kar do

    p1, p2 = head, second                  # 9: STEP C -- compare
    result = True                          # 10: assume palindrome
    while p2:                              # 11: second half chhoti ya barabar hai
        if p1.val != p2.val:               # 12: mismatch mila
            result = False                 # 13
            break                          # 14: aage compare karne ka fayda nahi
        p1 = p1.next                       # 15
        p2 = p2.next                       # 16

    slow.next = reverse_list(second)       # 17: STEP D -- list wapas jodo (restore)
    return result                          # 18


def reverse_list(node):
    prev = None                            # 19: reversed part ka head
    while node:                            # 20
        nxt = node.next                    # 21: agla yaad rakho, warna kho jaayega
        node.next = prev                   # 22: pointer ulta karo
        prev = node                        # 23: prev aage badhao
        node = nxt                         # 24: current aage badhao
    return prev                            # 25: naya head

Line by line — kyun aise likha hai

1-2. Guard clause. head is None (empty) aur head.next is None (single node) dono trivially palindrome hain. Yeh guard nahi hota toh line 4 fast.next par crash karti agar head None hota. 3. slow = fast = head. 4. while fast.next and fast.next.next: — dhyaan do, yeh Problem 3.3 se alag condition hai. Yahan fast.next se shuru kiya, fast se nahi. Iska effect: slow pehli half ke aakhri node par rukta hai, na ki middle par. - Length 4 (1,2,2,1): slow node 2 (index 1) par rukta hai — pehli half ka aakhri. slow.next = index 2 se second half. - Length 5 (1,2,3,2,1): slow node 3 (index 2, middle) par rukta hai. slow.next = index 3 se. Middle node kisi bhi half mein nahi jaata, jo odd-length palindrome ke liye exactly sahi hai (middle apne aap se match karta hai, compare karne ki zaroorat nahi). Line 1 ka guard is line ko safe banata hai kyunki head.next guaranteed exist karta hai. 5-6. Standard moves. 7. second = reverse_list(slow.next) — second half ko reverse karke uska naya head liya. 8. slow.next = None — yeh line optional lagti hai lekin zaroori hai. Reverse ke baad slow.next abhi bhi purane second-half ke pehle node ko point kar raha hai, jo ab reversed list ka aakhri node hai. Agar None nahi karein toh pehli half ka traversal second half mein ghus jaayega, aur worse — restore step confusing ho jaayega. Isko None karke hum do saaf, alag lists bana dete hain. 9. p1, p2 = head, second — do walkers. 10. result = True — seedha return False kyun nahi kiya line 13 par? Kyunki hum line 17 par list restore karna chahte hain. Beech mein return kar dete toh list permanently toot kar reversed reh jaati — jo caller ke liye ek side effect hai. Interview mein yeh mention karna bahut acha impression deta hai. 11. while p2: — p2 par loop karte hain, p1 par nahi. Odd length par pehli half ek node lambi hoti hai (middle uske paas hai), toh p1 pehle khatam nahi hoga. p2 khatam hone par compare poora ho chuka. 12-14. Mismatch → flag set, break. 15-16. Dono aage. 17. slow.next = reverse_list(second) — second half ko wapas seedha karke phir se joda. Ab original list bilkul pehle jaisi hai. 18. return result. 19. prev = None — reversed part shuru mein khaali hai, aur original head ka next None hona chahiye (kyunki woh naya tail banega). 20. while node: — jab tak node hai. 21. nxt = node.next — yeh line kyun pehle? Kyunki line 22 node.next ko overwrite kar degi. Agar 21 aur 22 ka order ulta kar dein toh nxt galat value le lega aur baaki list hamesha ke liye kho jaayegi. Yeh reversal ka sabse classic bug hai. 22. node.next = prev — asli reversal, arrow ulta. 23. prev = node — ab yeh node reversed part ka head hai. 24. node = nxt — saved reference se aage badho. 25. return prev — loop khatam hone par node None hai aur prev aakhri processed node, yaani naya head.

Dry run — 1 -> 2 -> 2 -> 1 (nodes A,B,C,D)

Step A (middle):

Iteration slow fast fast.next and fast.next.next? Action init A A A.next=B, B.next=C → Yes slow=B, fast=C 1 B C C.next=D, D.next=None → No stop

slow = B — pehli half ka aakhri node. Sahi.

Step B (reverse C -> D):

Iteration node prev nxt After: node.next New prev New node 1 C None D C.next = None C D 2 D C None D.next = C D None exit None D — — — —

second = D, list ab D -> C -> None. Aur slow.next = None se A -> B -> None.

Step C (compare):

Step p1 p2 p1.val p2.val Match? Action 1 A D 1 1 Yes p1=B, p2=C 2 B C 2 2 Yes p1=None, p2=None 3 None None — — — while p2 False → exit

result = True.

Step D (restore): reverse_list(D) → C -> D -> None, aur B.next = C. List wapas A->B->C->D. Return True.

Dry run — 1 -> 2 -> 3 (A,B,C) — expected False

Step A: init slow=A, fast=A. A.next=B exists, B.next=C exists → slow=B, fast=C. Ab C.next None → stop. slow = B (middle node 2).

Step B: reverse_list(C) → second = C. B.next = None. Lists: A->B, C.

Step C:

Step p1 p2 p1.val p2.val Match? 1 A C 1 3 No → result=False, break

Return False. Sahi — 1,2,3 palindrome nahi hai.

Complexity

  • Time: O(n). Middle dhoondhna n/2, reverse n/2, compare n/2, restore n/2 — total 2n, jo O(n) hai. Constant factor 2 hai lekin asymptotically linear.
  • Space: O(1). Sirf pointers. Yehi poori exercise ka point tha.

Edge cases

Case Input Output Kyun Empty None True Guard clause Single 1 True Guard clause Two same 1->1 True slow=A, second=B, ek compare Two different 1->2 False Pehle compare par mismatch Odd palindrome 1->2->1 True Middle node skip hota hai Even palindrome 1->2->2->1 True Upar dry run All same 5->5->5->5 True Long non-palindrome 1->2->3->4 False Pehla compare 1 vs 4

Variations

  • Restore mat karo — code 4 lines chhota, lekin caller ki list corrupt. Interview mein bolna: "I'd restore in production code because mutating the caller's input is a surprising side effect."
  • Doubly linked list — trivial ho jaata hai: do pointers, ek head se ek tail se, andar ki taraf chalao.
  • Recursion se — call stack ko "reverse traversal" ki tarah use karo. O(n) space (stack), lekin elegant.
  • Thread safety — agar list concurrently read ho rahi ho toh mutation-based solution safe nahi. Yeh QA/SDET mindset wala point hai aur interviewer ko pasand aata hai.
  • Palindrome check on a stream — possible nahi bina buffering ke.

Interview answer: "The straightforward solution copies the values into an array and compares it to its reverse. O(n) time, O(n) space.

To hit O(1) space I compose three things. First, fast and slow pointers to find the end of the first half — note I use a slightly different loop condition here than for finding the middle, so slow stops on the last node of the first half and the middle node of an odd list stays out of both halves, which is exactly right since a middle character always matches itself.

Second, I reverse the second half in place. Third, I walk both halves forward simultaneously and compare values. I loop on the second-half pointer because for odd lengths the first half is one node longer.

One thing I'd do deliberately: instead of returning false the moment I find a mismatch, I set a flag and break, then reverse the second half back and reattach it before returning. Mutating the caller's list and leaving it half-reversed is a nasty side effect — especially if anything else holds a reference to it. That restore step costs another n over two operations and keeps the function well-behaved.

O(n) time, O(1) space."

docs.title: Problem 3.6 — Find The Duplicate Number
docs.text:
Problem statement

Ek array nums hai jismein n + 1 integers hain, har value 1 se n ke beech (inclusive). Exactly ek value repeat hoti hai (kitni bhi baar). Woh duplicate lautao.

Constraints: array ko modify nahi kar sakte (read-only), aur sirf O(1) extra space use kar sakte ho.

Input: [1, 3, 4, 2, 2]     Output: 2
Input: [3, 1, 3, 4, 2]     Output: 3

Pehla instinct — brute force

Har element ke liye baaki sab check karo.

def find_duplicate_brute(nums):
    for i in range(len(nums)):            # 1: har element ke liye
        for j in range(i + 1, len(nums)): # 2: uske aage wale sab
            if nums[i] == nums[j]:        # 3: match mila
                return nums[i]            # 4
    return -1                             # 5: constraints ke hisaab se yahan nahi pahunchenge

Line by line — kyun aise likha hai

  1. for i in range(len(nums)) — outer loop.
  2. for j in range(i + 1, ...) — i + 1 se shuru, 0 se nahi. 0 se karte toh i == j par element khud se compare hota aur hamesha False answer aata. Aur har pair do baar check hota. 3-4. Match → answer.
  3. return -1 — defensive; problem guarantee deti hai ki duplicate hai, lekin function ko total banana acchi habit hai.

Complexity: Time O(n^2), Space O(1). Space theek hai, time bekaar.

Ek aur brute force — set

def find_duplicate_set(nums):
    seen = set()                          # 6: ab tak dekhe gaye
    for x in nums:                        # 7
        if x in seen:                     # 8: dobara mila
            return x                      # 9
        seen.add(x)                       # 10
    return -1                             # 11

Time O(n), lekin Space O(n) — jo constraint todta hai.

Ek aur — sorting

def find_duplicate_sort(nums):
    nums.sort()                           # 12: PROBLEM -- input modify kar diya
    for i in range(1, len(nums)):         # 13
        if nums[i] == nums[i - 1]:        # 14: sorted mein duplicates padosi hote hain
            return nums[i]                # 15
    return -1                             # 16

Time O(n log n), Space O(1) — lekin line 12 array modify karti hai, jo constraint todta hai.

Isme problem kya hai

Teenon approaches mein se har ek ek constraint todta hai: brute force time, set space, sort mutation. Interviewer specifically dono constraints ek saath maangta hai, aur yahi is problem ki poori difficulty hai.

The insight

Yeh problem ka sabse chhupa hua part hai, isliye dhyaan se.

Array ko ek function ki tarah dekho: index i se value nums[i] par jao. Yaani i -> nums[i]. Ab yeh ek "linked list" ban gaya jahan har index ek node hai aur nums[i] uska next hai.

Kyun yeh valid hai? Kyunki values 1 se n ke beech hain aur indices 0 se n tak — toh har value ek valid index hai (0 ko chhod kar, aur 0 kabhi value nahi hai toh 0 par koi wapas nahi aata). Matlab index 0 se shuru karna hamesha safe hai aur woh cycle ka hissa nahi ban sakta — exactly linked list ke tail jaisa jo cycle mein le jaata hai.

Ab: duplicate value ka matlab hai ki do alag indices ek hi jagah point karte hain — yaani us node ke do incoming arrows hain. Aur linked-list-with-cycle mein exactly wahi node cycle ka entry point hota hai jiske do incoming arrows hain.

Toh: duplicate number = cycle ka start = Floyd ka phase 2 ka answer. Poori problem Problem 3.2 ban gayi.

Optimal solution

def find_duplicate(nums):
    slow = nums[0]                        # 1: index 0 se ek step -- yaani nums[0]
    fast = nums[nums[0]]                  # 2: index 0 se do step
    while slow != fast:                   # 3: PHASE 1 -- meeting point dhoondo
        slow = nums[slow]                 # 4: ek step
        fast = nums[nums[fast]]           # 5: do step

    slow = 0                              # 6: PHASE 2 -- ek pointer start (index 0) par
    while slow != fast:                   # 7: dono ab same speed
        slow = nums[slow]                 # 8
        fast = nums[fast]                 # 9
    return slow                           # 10: cycle ka entry = duplicate value

Line by line — kyun aise likha hai

  1. slow = nums[0] — index 0 se ek step chal chuke. Note: hum pointer ko "current index" ki tarah rakh rahe hain, aur nums[current] uska next hai.
  2. fast = nums[nums[0]] — index 0 se do step. Dono ko 0 par rakhna galat hota kyunki line 3 shuru mein equality check karti hai (wahi issue jo Problem 3.4 mein tha).
  3. while slow != fast: — meeting point tak.
  4. slow = nums[slow] — ek application.
  5. fast = nums[nums[fast]] — do application. Nested indexing hi "double speed" hai.
  6. slow = 0 — 0 par reset, nums[0] par nahi. Floyd ka formula F = head se entry tak ki distance maangta hai, aur yahan head index 0 hai. Yahan galti karna common hai.
  7. while slow != fast: — dono equal speed. 8-9. Dono ek ek step.
  8. return slow — yeh value hai (kyunki slow ek index hai aur wahi index duplicate value ke barabar hai — entry point ka index hi woh value hai jispe do arrows aate hain). Confusing lagta hai lekin sahi hai: cycle ka entry "node" number d hai, aur node number hi array ki value hai.

Ek sawaal jo poocha jaata hai: "0 cycle ka hissa kyun nahi ban sakta?" Kyunki cycle mein aane ke liye kisi i ke liye nums[i] = 0 hona chahiye. Lekin constraint kehti hai values 1 se n hain, 0 kabhi value nahi hai. Toh index 0 ke koi incoming arrow nahi hai, matlab woh hamesha "tail" par hai, cycle ke bahar. Yehi guarantee hai ki hum index 0 se safely start kar sakte hain.

Dry run — nums = [1, 3, 4, 2, 2]

Mapping (index → value): 0→1, 1→3, 2→4, 3→2, 4→2. Chalke dekho: 0 → 1 → 3 → 2 → 4 → 2 → 4 → ... Cycle {2, 4}, entry 2. Expected answer 2.

Phase 1:

Step slow fast Equal? Next slow Next fast init nums[0]=1 nums[nums[0]]=nums[1]=3 No — — 1 1 3 No nums[1]=3 nums[nums[3]]=nums[2]=4 2 3 4 No nums[3]=2 nums[nums[4]]=nums[2]=4 3 2 4 No nums[2]=4 nums[nums[4]]=nums[2]=4 4 4 4 Yes → exit — —

Meeting at 4.

Phase 2:

Step slow fast Equal? Action init 0 4 No slow=nums[0]=1, fast=nums[4]=2 1 1 2 No slow=nums[1]=3, fast=nums[2]=4 2 3 4 No slow=nums[3]=2, fast=nums[4]=2 3 2 2 Yes → exit return 2

Answer: 2. Sahi.

Complexity

  • Time: O(n). Do phases, dono linear.
  • Space: O(1). Do integer variables. Array touch nahi hota — read-only constraint respected.

Edge cases

Case Input Output Note Minimum size [1, 1] 1 n=1, array size 2 Duplicate at start [2, 2, 2, 2, 2] 2 Cycle length 1 Duplicate repeats many times [1, 1, 1, 1] 1 Algorithm frequency se independent hai Duplicate at end [1, 2, 3, 4, 4] 4 Long cycle [3, 1, 3, 4, 2] 3 Sorted-ish [1, 2, 3, 3] 3

Variations

  • Binary search on the answer — count karo kitne numbers <= mid hain; agar count > mid toh duplicate [1, mid] mein hai. O(n log n) time, O(1) space, array read-only. Yeh alternative bhi bolna acha hai; Section 11 mein detail.
  • Bit manipulation counting — har bit position par count compare karo. O(32n), thoda exotic.
  • Agar mutation allowed ho — negative marking: nums[abs(x)] ko negate karo, jo pehle se negative hai wahi duplicate. O(n) time, O(1) space, lekin array modify.
  • Ek se zyada duplicates — Floyd fail ho jaata hai (multiple cycles); tab set ya sorting.
  • Missing number bhi chahiye (LeetCode 645) — cyclic sort pattern, Section 5 dekho.

Interview answer: "Three obvious approaches each break one of the constraints: nested loops are O(n squared), a hash set is O(n) space, and sorting mutates the input. To satisfy both constraints I need the trick.

The reframe is to treat the array as a function from index to value — index i points to index nums[i]. Because every value is between 1 and n and the indices go 0 to n, every value is a valid index, so this is a well-defined linked list where each node has exactly one next.

Two facts follow. Index zero can never be pointed at, since zero is never a value — so it's outside any cycle, which makes it a valid starting head. And a duplicated value means two different indices point at the same place, which is precisely a node with two incoming arrows — the entry point of a cycle.

So the duplicate is the cycle entry, and that's Floyd's algorithm. Phase one finds a meeting point with a one-step and two-step pointer. Phase two resets one pointer to index zero — not to nums[0] — and advances both at the same speed until they collide. Where they collide is the duplicate.

O(n) time, O(1) space, and the array is never written to.

If the interviewer wants a second option, binary searching on the value range also works: for a candidate mid, count how many elements are at most mid — if that count exceeds mid, the duplicate is in the lower half. That's O(n log n) but much easier to explain."

docs.title: Problem 3.7 — Reorder List
docs.text:
Problem statement

List L0 -> L1 -> ... -> Ln-1 -> Ln ko is order mein reorder karo: L0 -> Ln -> L1 -> Ln-1 -> L2 -> ... Values change nahi karni, sirf nodes ke links.

Input:  1 -> 2 -> 3 -> 4          Output: 1 -> 4 -> 2 -> 3
Input:  1 -> 2 -> 3 -> 4 -> 5     Output: 1 -> 5 -> 2 -> 4 -> 3

Pehla instinct — brute force

Saare nodes ek array mein, phir do pointers (start aur end) se naya order banao.

def reorder_brute(head):
    if not head:                          # 1: empty guard
        return
    nodes = []                            # 2: sab nodes ka array
    current = head                        # 3
    while current:                        # 4
        nodes.append(current)             # 5: NODE store kar rahe hain, value nahi
        current = current.next            # 6
    i, j = 0, len(nodes) - 1              # 7: do ends
    while i < j:                          # 8: jab tak cross na karein
        nodes[i].next = nodes[j]          # 9: front node ko back node se jodo
        i += 1                            # 10: front aage
        if i == j:                        # 11: beech mein mil gaye -> khatam
            break                         # 12
        nodes[j].next = nodes[i]          # 13: back node ko naye front se jodo
        j -= 1                            # 14: back peeche
    nodes[j].next = None                  # 15: aakhri node ka next terminate karo

Line by line — kyun aise likha hai

  1. Empty guard.
  2. nodes = [] — values nahi, actual node objects. Kyunki hume links badalne hain, naye nodes nahi banane. 3-6. Sab nodes collect.
  3. i, j = 0, len(nodes) - 1 — classic two-pointer ends.
  4. while i < j: — strict <, kyunki i == j par ek hi node hai aur usko khud se jodna galat hoga.
  5. nodes[i].next = nodes[j] — pehla → aakhri.
  6. i += 1. 11-12. if i == j: break — yeh check zaroori hai. Odd length mein i badhne ke baad j par pahunch sakta hai; tab line 13 nodes[j].next = nodes[j] kar deti aur self-loop ban jaata — infinite list.
  7. nodes[j].next = nodes[i] — aakhri → dusra.
  8. j -= 1.
  9. nodes[j].next = None — poori list ka tail terminate karna. Yeh bhool jaana sabse common bug hai; bina iske list mein cycle reh jaata hai.

Complexity: Time O(n), Space O(n) — array ki wajah se.

Isme problem kya hai

O(n) space. Aur yeh problem specifically "compose three patterns in O(1) space" test hai — bilkul Problem 3.5 jaisa.

The insight

Target order dekho: L0, Ln, L1, Ln-1, ... — yeh exactly pehli half aur reversed second half ka alternating merge hai.

1 2 3 4 → pehli half 1 2, second half reversed 4 3 → interleave → 1 4 2 3. Sahi.

Toh teen steps: middle dhoondo (fast/slow) → second half reverse karo → do lists ko alternate karke merge karo. Teenon O(1) space mein hote hain.

Optimal solution

def reorder_list(head):
    if head is None or head.next is None:  # 1: 0 ya 1 node -> kuch nahi karna
        return                             # 2

    slow = fast = head                     # 3: STEP A -- pehli half ka aakhri node
    while fast.next and fast.next.next:    # 4
        slow = slow.next                   # 5
        fast = fast.next.next              # 6

    second = slow.next                     # 7: second half ka pehla node
    slow.next = None                       # 8: halves alag karo -- ZAROORI
    prev = None                            # 9: STEP B -- second half reverse
    while second:                          # 10
        nxt = second.next                  # 11: agla bachao
        second.next = prev                 # 12: arrow ulta
        prev = second                      # 13
        second = nxt                       # 14
    second = prev                          # 15: reversed second half ka head

    first = head                           # 16: STEP C -- alternating merge
    while second:                          # 17: second chhoti ya barabar hai
        f_next = first.next                # 18: dono ke next bachao
        s_next = second.next               # 19
        first.next = second                # 20: first -> second
        second.next = f_next               # 21: second -> first ka purana next
        first = f_next                     # 22: dono ko aage badhao
        second = s_next                    # 23

Line by line — kyun aise likha hai

1-2. Guard. return (bina value) kyunki problem in-place modification maangti hai, naya head nahi. 3-6. Problem 3.5 wali hi condition — slow pehli half ke aakhri node par rukta hai. Odd length par middle node pehli half mein rehta hai, jo yahan sahi hai: 1 2 3 4 5 → pehli half 1 2 3, second half 4 5 → reversed 5 4 → merge 1 5 2 4 3. Exactly expected output. 7. second = slow.next. 8. slow.next = None — agar yeh line hata do toh line 20-21 ka merge ek cycle bana dega, kyunki pehli half ka tail abhi bhi second half ke andar point kar raha hoga. Yeh sabse mehnga bug hai kyunki test infinite loop mein chala jaata hai. 9-15. In-place reversal. Line 11 (nxt pehle bachao) ka reason wahi hai jo Problem 3.5 mein tha — line 12 second.next ko destroy kar deti hai. 15. second = prev — variable reuse. Chahe toh alag naam de sakte the (second_head), lekin prev hi naya head hai. 16. first = head. 17. while second: — second par loop. Odd length par pehli half ek node lambi hoti hai. Jab second khatam ho jaayega, first ke paas ek node bacha hoga jiska next pehle se hi None hai (line 8 ki wajah se) — toh woh natural tail ban jaata hai. Isliye end mein alag se terminate karne ki zaroorat nahi. 18-19. Dono next pehle save karo. Line 20 first.next destroy karti hai aur line 21 second.next. Agar save nahi karein toh dono raaste kho jaayenge. Order 18→19→20→21 hi safe hai. 20. first.next = second — interleave ka pehla arrow. 21. second.next = f_next — interleave ka dusra arrow. 22-23. Dono aage.

Kyun end mein tail terminate karne ki zaroorat nahi: even length 1 2 3 4 → halves 1 2 aur 4 3. Merge ke baad 1 -> 4 -> 2 -> 3. Node 3 ka next reversal ke baad None tha (kyunki reversal mein pehla node naya tail banta hai aur uska next prev = None set hota hai). Odd length 1 2 3 4 5 → halves 1 2 3 aur 5 4. Merge: 1->5->2->4->3, aur 3 ka next line 8 se None hai. Dono cases covered.

Dry run — 1 -> 2 -> 3 -> 4 (nodes A,B,C,D)

Step A:

Iteration slow fast fast.next and fast.next.next? Action init A A B aur C exist → Yes slow=B, fast=C 1 B C C.next=D, D.next=None → No stop

slow = B. second = C. B.next = None. Lists: A->B, C->D.

Step B (reverse C->D):

Iter second prev nxt Action New prev New second 1 C None D C.next = None C D 2 D C None D.next = C D None

second = D, list D->C->None.

Step C (merge A->B with D->C):

Iter first second f_next s_next Links set New first New second 1 A D B C A.next=D, D.next=B B C 2 B C None None B.next=C, C.next=None None None exit — None — — — — —

Final list: A(1) -> D(4) -> B(2) -> C(3) -> None = 1 -> 4 -> 2 -> 3. Sahi.

Dry run — 1 -> 2 -> 3 -> 4 -> 5 (A..E)

Step A: init slow=A, fast=A → B, C exist → slow=B, fast=C. Next: C.next=D, D.next=E exist → slow=C, fast=E. Next: E.next None → stop. slow = C. second = D, C.next = None. Lists: A->B->C, D->E.

Step B: reverse D->E → E->D->None. second = E.

Step C:

Iter first second f_next s_next Links New first New second 1 A E B D A.next=E, E.next=B B D 2 B D C None B.next=D, D.next=C C None exit C None — — — — —

Final: 1 -> 5 -> 2 -> 4 -> 3, aur C(3).next None hai (step A ki line 8 se). Sahi.

Complexity

  • Time: O(n). Teen linear passes → 3n → O(n).
  • Space: O(1). Sirf pointers.

Edge cases

Case Input Behaviour Kyun Empty None Return, no change Guard Single 1 1 Guard Two 1->2 1->2 slow=A, second=B, reverse=B, merge: A.next=B, B.next=None Three 1->2->3 1->3->2 Four 1->2->3->4 1->4->2->3 Upar All same values 5->5->5 5->5->5 Structure badal jaata hai, values same dikhti hain

Variations

  • Ulta reorder — L0 -> Ln -> Ln-1 -> ... yeh alag problem hai (concat, not interleave).
  • Odd/even indexed nodes alag karo (LeetCode 328) — same "split and reattach" skill.
  • Swap nodes in pairs (24) — chhota version.
  • Rotate list (61) — length count plus cut.
  • Return naya head instead of in-place — head kabhi change nahi hota is problem mein, isliye function None return karta hai.

Interview answer: "The target order — first, last, second, second-last — is exactly what you get by interleaving the first half of the list with the reversed second half. Once I see that, the solution is three standard steps, each O(1) space.

One: find the end of the first half with fast and slow pointers, using the condition that leaves the middle node in the first half for odd lengths — which is what this ordering wants.

Two: cut the list in two by nulling the first half's tail, then reverse the second half in place. Cutting is not optional — if I skip it, the merge creates a cycle because the first half still points into the second.

Three: interleave. In the merge loop I save both next pointers before rewiring, because each assignment destroys one of them.

The loop runs on the second-half pointer since the first half can be one node longer. And I don't need to null the final tail explicitly — for even lengths the reversal already left it null, and for odd lengths the cut in step two did.

O(n) time, O(1) space. The array-of-nodes version is O(n) space and much easier to write, and I'd offer that first if the interviewer just wants something working."
