    # via pytest

    # via pytest

    # via -r requirements.in

    # via pytest

    # via playwright
pytest==8.0.0
    # via
    #   -r requirements.in
    #   pytest-html

...

Kyun do files:

  1. requirements.in mein aapki intent hai — kaunse packages aapko chahiye aur kyun.
  2. requirements.txt lock file hai — exact versions, including transitive dependencies. Ye reproducible builds deta hai.
  3. pip-compile (pip-tools se) ya uv pip compile .in se .txt generate karta hai.
  4. # via pytest comments batate hain ki har transitive dependency kyun hai — ye debugging mein invaluable hai.

Bina lock file ke kya hota hai:

Aap:      pip install pytest>=7.4        -> pytest 8.0.0 mila
CI (kal):  pip install pytest>=7.4       -> pytest 8.1.0 mila (naya release)
           -> ek plugin incompatible -> saare tests fail
           -> aur ye aapke code change se bilkul unrelated hai

Multiple environments:

requirements/
├── base.in           # core dependencies
├── base.txt
├── dev.in            # -r base.in + pytest, ruff, mypy
├── dev.txt
├── ci.in             # -r base.in + pytest-xdist, coverage
└── ci.txt

# dev.in
-r base.in
ruff>=0.2
mypy>=1.8
ipdb

docs.title: pyproject.toml — modern standard
docs.text:
pyproject.toml ek file hai jo setup.py, setup.cfg, requirements.txt, aur saare tool configs ko replace kar deti hai.

# ============ BUILD SYSTEM ============
[build-system]
requires = ["setuptools>=68", "wheel"]
build-backend = "setuptools.build_meta"

# ============ PROJECT METADATA (PEP 621) ============
[project]
name = "qa-framework"
version = "1.2.0"
description = "Playwright + pytest test automation framework"
readme = "README.md"
requires-python = ">=3.11"
license = {text = "MIT"}
authors = [{name = "Ritik Chaturvedi", email = "ritik.chaturvedi@merlinai.co"}]
keywords = ["testing", "playwright", "pytest", "automation"]
classifiers = [
    "Development Status :: 4 - Beta",
    "Framework :: Pytest",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.11",
]

dependencies = [
    "playwright>=1.40,<2.0",
    "pytest>=7.4",
    "pyyaml>=6.0",
    "requests>=2.31",
]

[project.optional-dependencies]
dev = [
    "ruff>=0.2",
    "mypy>=1.8",
    "types-requests",
    "types-PyYAML",
    "ipdb",
]
ci = [
    "pytest-xdist>=3.5",
    "pytest-html>=4.1",
    "pytest-cov>=4.1",
    "pytest-rerunfailures>=13.0",
]

[project.scripts]
qa-report = "qa_framework.cli:main"          # 'qa-report' command banata hai

[project.urls]
Repository = "https://github.com/company/qa-framework"

# ============ SETUPTOOLS CONFIG ============
[tool.setuptools.packages.find]
where = ["src"]

# ============ PYTEST ============
[tool.pytest.ini_options]
minversion = "7.0"
testpaths = ["tests"]
python_files = ["test_*.py"]
python_classes = ["Test*"]
python_functions = ["test_*"]
addopts = [
    "-ra",                              # summary of all except passed
    "--strict-markers",                 # undefined marker = error
    "--strict-config",                  # config warning = error
    "--import-mode=importlib",
    "--tb=short",
]
markers = [
    "smoke: quick sanity checks",
    "regression: full regression suite",
    "slow: takes more than 30 seconds",
    "flaky: known to be intermittent",
]
filterwarnings = [
    "error",                            # warnings ko errors banao
    "ignore::DeprecationWarning:playwright.*",
]
log_cli = true
log_cli_level = "INFO"

# ============ RUFF (linter + formatter) ============
[tool.ruff]
line-length = 100
target-version = "py311"
src = ["src", "tests"]

[tool.ruff.lint]
select = [
    "E", "W",      # pycodestyle
    "F",           # pyflakes
    "I",           # isort
    "N",           # pep8-naming
    "UP",          # pyupgrade
    "B",           # flake8-bugbear (mutable defaults, etc.)
    "A",           # flake8-builtins (shadowing)
    "C4",          # flake8-comprehensions
    "SIM",         # flake8-simplify
    "PT",          # flake8-pytest-style
    "RET",         # flake8-return
    "S",           # flake8-bandit (security)
]
ignore = [
    "S101",        # assert use -- tests mein zaruri hai
    "E501",        # line length -- formatter handle karta hai
]

[tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores]
"tests/**" = ["S105", "S106"]          # hardcoded passwords test data mein OK

[tool.ruff.lint.isort]
known-first-party = ["qa_framework"]

# ============ MYPY ============
[tool.mypy]
python_version = "3.11"
strict = true
warn_return_any = true
warn_unused_configs = true
show_error_codes = true

[[tool.mypy.overrides]]
module = ["pytest_html.*", "some_untyped_lib.*"]
ignore_missing_imports = true

# ============ COVERAGE ============
[tool.coverage.run]
source = ["src/qa_framework"]
branch = true
omit = ["*/tests/*", "*/__main__.py"]

[tool.coverage.report]
precision = 2
show_missing = true
skip_covered = false
exclude_lines = [
    "pragma: no cover",
    "if TYPE_CHECKING:",
    "raise NotImplementedError",
    "if __name__ == .__main__.:",
]

Key sections ka explanation:

  1. [build-system] — PEP 517/518. Ye batata hai ki package build karne ke liye kya chahiye. Iske bina pip install -e . legacy setup.py mode use karta hai.
  2. [project] — PEP 621 standard metadata. Pehle ye setup.py mein Python code tha; ab declarative hai.
  3. dependencies — runtime dependencies, loose ranges ke saath. Lock file alag rehti hai (requirements.txt ya uv.lock).
  4. [project.optional-dependencies] — extras. pip install -e ".[dev,ci]" se install hote hain. Ye requirements-dev.txt se better hai kyunki sab ek jagah hai.
  5. [project.scripts] — console entry points. Install ke baad qa-report command available ho jaati hai.
  6. addopts = ["--strict-markers"] — ye zaruri hai: typo wala marker (@pytest.mark.smok) silently ignore hone ki jagah error dega.
  7. filterwarnings = ["error"] — warnings ko errors banao. Ye deprecations ko chhupne nahi deta — jab library upgrade ho toh aapko turant pata chalega.
  8. [tool.ruff.lint] select = [...] — ruff 800+ rules implement karta hai flake8 plugins se. B (bugbear) mutable defaults pakadta hai, A builtin shadowing, S security issues.
  9. per-file-ignores — tests mein assert (S101) aur hardcoded test passwords (S105) allowed hain, production code mein nahi.
  10. branch = true coverage mein — branch coverage bhi measure karo, sirf line coverage nahi. if x: ke dono raaste chale ya nahi.

docs.title: pip install -e . — editable install
docs.text:
pip install -e .

Kya karta hai:

  1. Package ko site-packages mein copy nahi karta — ek link/path entry banata hai.
  2. Aapke source edits turant effective hote hain, dobara install nahi karna padta.
  3. src/ layout ke saath ye zaruri hai — warna import qa_framework kaam nahi karega.

Kyun sys.path hack se better:

# BURA -- conftest.py mein
import sys
from pathlib import Path
sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).parent.parent / "src"))     # hack

# ACHHA
# pip install -e .   (ek baar), phir normal imports

sys.path hack fragile hai, IDE confuse hoti hai, aur CI mein alag behave karta hai.

docs.title: Reproducible CI setup
docs.text:
# .github/workflows/tests.yml
- uses: actions/setup-python@v5
  with:
    python-version: "3.11"
    cache: "pip"                              # pip cache reuse karo

- run: pip install -r requirements.txt        # LOCK file se, pyproject se nahi
- run: pip install -e . --no-deps             # apna package, deps already installed
- run: playwright install --with-deps chromium
- run: pytest -n auto --html=report.html
  1. requirements.txt (lock) se install — exact versions, reproducible.
  2. --no-deps apne package ke liye — deps already lock se aa chuke hain.
  3. cache: "pip" — CI time bachaata hai.

Interview answer: "A virtual environment isolates a project's dependencies. Mechanically python -m venv .venv creates a directory with a symlink to the system interpreter and its own site-packages; the interpreter reads pyvenv.cfg and sets sys.prefix, which is what redirects imports. activate just prepends the venv's bin to PATH — in CI I skip it and call .venv/bin/python directly, so nothing depends on shell state.

For dependencies I keep two layers. pyproject.toml declares intent with loose ranges, plus optional-dependency groups for dev and CI, and a lock file — generated with pip-compile or uv — pins exact versions including transitives. Without the lock, a patch release of a pytest plugin can break the build on a day nobody touched the code, and that's the hardest kind of failure to explain. pyproject.toml also holds every tool's config: pytest markers with --strict-markers so a typo'd marker errors instead of silently doing nothing, filterwarnings = ["error"] so deprecations surface at upgrade time rather than at removal time, ruff's rule selection, mypy settings, and coverage with branch coverage on. And the project itself goes in with pip install -e ., which is what makes a src/ layout importable without any sys.path manipulation in conftest."

Cross-question — "Why src/ layout instead of putting the package at the repo root?" "Because with a flat layout the package directory is on sys.path implicitly — it's the current working directory — so your tests import the source tree directly and pass even if the packaging is broken. Classic failures that hides: a missing __init__.py, a data file not listed in package data, a module you forgot to include. With src/, the package isn't importable until it's actually installed, so pip install -e . is required and your tests run against the same import path a user would get. It also stops accidental imports of top-level repo files — a conftest.py or utils.py at the root can't shadow anything. The cost is one extra install step, which is trivial next to shipping a package that only works from a checkout."

Mode Meaning File nahi hai File hai Position r read (default) FileNotFoundError read karo start w write banao TRUNCATE (sab mit gaya!) start a append banao rakho end x exclusive create banao FileExistsError start r+ read + write FileNotFoundError rakho start w+ write + read banao TRUNCATE start a+ append + read banao rakho end x+ exclusive create + read banao FileExistsError start

Plus modifiers:

Modifier Meaning t text mode (default) — str deta hai, newlines translate hote hain b binary mode — bytes deta hai, koi translation nahi 
# Common combinations
open("f.txt")               # 'rt'  -- read text
open("f.txt", "w")          # 'wt'  -- write text (TRUNCATES!)
open("f.txt", "a")          # 'at'  -- append text
open("f.bin", "rb")         # read binary
open("f.bin", "wb")         # write binary
open("f.txt", "x")          # create only -- exists toh error

w ka khatra:

# BUG: ye poori file mita deta hai, chahe aap kuch likho ya na likho
with open("important_results.json", "w") as f:
    if some_condition:
        json.dump(data, f)
# Agar some_condition False hai -> file KHAALI ho gayi, data gaya

Fix — atomic write pattern:

import json
import os
import tempfile
from pathlib import Path


def write_json_atomic(path: Path, data: dict) -> None:
    """
    Ya toh poora naya content likho, ya original ko chhoo bhi mat.
    Crash/interrupt ke beech mein bhi file corrupt nahi hoti.
    """
    path = Path(path)
    tmp_fd, tmp_name = tempfile.mkstemp(
        dir=path.parent,                          # SAME filesystem par (rename atomic ho)
        prefix=f".{path.name}.",
        suffix=".tmp",
    )
    try:
        with os.fdopen(tmp_fd, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
            json.dump(data, f, indent=2)
            f.flush()                             # Python buffer -> OS buffer
            os.fsync(f.fileno())                  # OS buffer -> DISK
        os.replace(tmp_name, path)                # ATOMIC rename
    except BaseException:
        os.unlink(tmp_name)                       # cleanup temp file
        raise


write_json_atomic(Path("results.json"), {"tests": 42, "passed": 40})
print(Path("results.json").read_text())

Line-by-line walkthrough:

  1. tempfile.mkstemp(dir=path.parent, ...) — temp file usi directory mein banayi. Zaruri hai kyunki os.replace atomic sirf same filesystem par hota hai. /tmp alag filesystem ho sakta hai — tab rename ek copy+delete ban jaata hai, jo atomic nahi.
  2. prefix=f".{path.name}." — dot se shuru, toh hidden file. Agar crash ho jaaye toh directory listing mein noise nahi.
  3. os.fdopen(tmp_fd, "w", ...) — mkstemp ek file descriptor (int) deta hai, file object nahi. fdopen usko wrap karta hai.
  4. f.flush() — Python ka internal buffer OS ko de do.
  5. os.fsync(f.fileno()) — OS ko disk par likhne ko force karo. flush sirf OS buffer tak pahunchata hai; power failure par wo data ja sakta hai. Ye durability ke liye zaruri hai.
  6. os.replace(tmp_name, path) — atomic rename. POSIX aur Windows dono par atomic hai (os.rename Windows par existing file par fail karta hai, os.replace nahi).
  7. except BaseException: — yahan BaseException sahi hai kyunki KeyboardInterrupt par bhi temp file clean honi chahiye, aur raise se wo aage jaati hai.
  8. Ye pattern kab chahiye: test results, config files, kuch bhi jo aap CI mein likhte ho aur jo interrupt ho sakta hai.

docs.title: Buffering aur flush
docs.text:
# 1. Default buffering
with open("log.txt", "w") as f:
    f.write("line 1\n")                    # abhi buffer mein hai, disk par nahi
    # crash yahan -> "line 1" GAYA
# 'with' exit par flush + close hota hai

# 2. Line buffering -- har newline par flush
with open("log.txt", "w", buffering=1) as f:      # sirf TEXT mode mein
    f.write("line 1\n")                    # turant flush

# 3. Unbuffered (sirf binary mode)
with open("log.bin", "wb", buffering=0) as f:
    f.write(b"data")                       # turant disk par

# 4. Explicit flush
with open("log.txt", "w") as f:
    f.write("critical\n")
    f.flush()                              # ab OS ke paas hai
    os.fsync(f.fileno())                   # ab DISK par hai

QA use case: long-running test suite ka log. Agar suite crash ho jaaye toh aapko last lines chahiye. buffering=1 (line buffered) ya periodic flush() zaruri hai.

docs.title: Reading patterns
docs.text:
from pathlib import Path

p = Path("test_results.log")

# 1. Poori file ek string mein -- CHHOTI files ke liye
content = p.read_text(encoding="utf-8")

# 2. Lines ki list -- chhoti files
lines = p.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines()

# 3. Line-by-line, LAZY -- BADI files ke liye (Part 6)
with p.open(encoding="utf-8") as f:
    for line in f:                          # ek line at a time, buffered
        process(line)

# 4. Fixed-size chunks -- binary ya bahut badi files
with p.open("rb") as f:
    while chunk := f.read(65536):           # 64 KB chunks
        process_chunk(chunk)

# 5. Specific bytes/lines
with p.open(encoding="utf-8") as f:
    header = f.readline()                   # ek line
    f.seek(0)                                # wapas shuru
    first_100 = f.read(100)                  # 100 characters (text mode)

# 6. Aakhri N lines efficiently (tail)
from collections import deque
with p.open(encoding="utf-8") as f:
    last_50 = deque(f, maxlen=50)           # sirf 50 lines memory mein (3.6.3)

Line-by-line walkthrough:

  1. p.read_text(encoding="utf-8") — file kholta hai, poora padhta hai, band karta hai. Ek line mein — with open(...) as f: f.read() se saaf.
  2. for line in f: — file object iterator hai, internally buffered chunks padhta hai aur lines mein todta hai. readlines() (jo poori list banata hai) se bahut better hai bade files par.
  3. while chunk := f.read(65536): — walrus + chunked reading. 64 KB ek achha chunk size hai (typical filesystem block size ka multiple).
  4. f.seek(0) — position reset. Text mode mein seek sirf tell() se mili values ya 0 accept karta hai — kyunki multi-byte characters mein arbitrary offset invalid ho sakta hai.
  5. deque(f, maxlen=50) — ye ek beautiful idiom hai: poori file padhi jaati hai par sirf aakhri 50 lines memory mein rehti hain. Bounded deque automatically purane drop karta hai.

import os
import os.path
from pathlib import Path

# --- os.path: string manipulation, functions bikhre hue ---
base = "/home/ritik/project"
artifacts = os.path.join(base, "artifacts", "screenshots")
os.makedirs(artifacts, exist_ok=True)
files = [os.path.join(artifacts, f) for f in os.listdir(artifacts)
         if f.endswith(".png") and os.path.isfile(os.path.join(artifacts, f))]
name = os.path.splitext(os.path.basename(files[0]))[0] if files else None

# --- pathlib: objects, methods chained ---
base = Path("/home/ritik/project")
artifacts = base / "artifacts" / "screenshots"
artifacts.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

Farak:

  2. Methods object par hain — f.is_file() vs os.path.isfile(f). IDE autocomplete kaam karta hai.
  3. Path ek object hai, string nahi — toh type checker galtiyaan pakad sakta hai.
  4. Cross-platform — Path OS ke hisaab se WindowsPath ya PosixPath banata hai.

docs.title: QA use cases
docs.text:
1. Project root reliably nikaalna

from pathlib import Path

# BURA -- CWD par depend karta hai
ROOT = Path(".")                                   # kahan se command chali, uspar depend

# ACHHA -- file ki location par based
ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent      # conftest.py se do level upar

# BEHTAR -- marker file dhoondho
def find_project_root(start: Path | None = None, markers=("pyproject.toml", ".git")) -> Path:
    """Upar chalte jao jab tak marker file na mile."""
    current = (start or Path(__file__)).resolve()
    for parent in [current, *current.parents]:
        if any((parent / m).exists() for m in markers):
            return parent
    raise FileNotFoundError(f"no project root found above {current} (looked for {markers})")

ROOT = find_project_root()
ARTIFACTS = ROOT / "artifacts"
TEST_DATA = ROOT / "tests" / "data"

Line-by-line walkthrough:

  1. Path(__file__).resolve() — resolve() symlinks resolve karta hai aur absolute banata hai. Bina resolve() ke, agar script symlink se chali toh parent galat ho sakta hai.
  2. for parent in [current, *current.parents]: — khud se shuru karke upar. current.parents ek sequence hai jo root tak jaati hai.
  3. any((parent / m).exists() for m in markers) — generator, short-circuits.
  4. Ye pattern robust hai: chahe test kahin se bhi chale, root sahi milta hai.

2. Artifacts organise karna

from pathlib import Path
from datetime import datetime


class ArtifactStore:
    """Test artifacts ko structured tareeke se rakho."""

    def __init__(self, root: Path, run_id: str | None = None):
        self.run_id = run_id or datetime.now().strftime("%Y%m%d_%H%M%S")
        self.root = Path(root) / self.run_id
        self.root.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    def path_for(self, test_name: str, kind: str, ext: str) -> Path:
        """artifacts/20260823_140000/screenshots/test_login.png"""
        safe_name = "".join(c if c.isalnum() or c in "-_." else "_" for c in test_name)
        subdir = self.root / kind
        subdir.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
        return subdir / f"{safe_name}.{ext.lstrip('.')}"

    def screenshot(self, test_name: str) -> Path:
        return self.path_for(test_name, "screenshots", "png")

    def trace(self, test_name: str) -> Path:
        return self.path_for(test_name, "traces", "zip")

    def cleanup_old_runs(self, keep: int = 10) -> list[Path]:
        """Purane runs delete karo, aakhri N rakho."""
        import shutil
        runs = sorted(
            (d for d in self.root.parent.iterdir() if d.is_dir()),
            key=lambda d: d.stat().st_mtime,
            reverse=True,
        )
        removed = []
        for old in runs[keep:]:
            shutil.rmtree(old, ignore_errors=True)
            removed.append(old)
        return removed


store = ArtifactStore(Path("artifacts"))
print(store.screenshot("test_login[chromium-staging]"))
# artifacts/20260823_140523/screenshots/test_login_chromium-staging_.png

Line-by-line walkthrough:

  1. datetime.now().strftime("%Y%m%d_%H%M%S") — sortable timestamp. %Y%m%d format lexically sort hota hai — ye deliberate choice hai.
  2. "".join(c if c.isalnum() or c in "-_." else "_" for c in test_name) — filename sanitisation. pytest test IDs mein [, ], /, : hote hain jo filenames mein illegal ya problematic hain (: Windows par illegal, / path separator).
  3. ext.lstrip('.') — caller "png" ya ".png" dono de sakta hai.
  4. sorted(..., key=lambda d: d.stat().st_mtime, reverse=True) — newest first.
  5. shutil.rmtree(old, ignore_errors=True) — recursive delete. ignore_errors=True isliye ki ek locked file poore cleanup ko na rok de.

3. Test data files dhoondhna

from pathlib import Path

TEST_DATA = Path(__file__).parent / "data"


def load_fixture(name: str) -> str:
    """Test data file padho, achhi error ke saath agar na mile."""
    path = TEST_DATA / name
    if not path.exists():
        available = sorted(p.name for p in TEST_DATA.iterdir() if p.is_file())
        raise FileNotFoundError(
            f"fixture {name!r} not found in {TEST_DATA}. Available: {available}"
        )
    return path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")

available list error message mein — typo turant pakda jaata hai.

docs.title: Gotchas
docs.text:
Gotcha 1 — Path string nahi hai.

from pathlib import Path
p = Path("/tmp/x.txt")
# subprocess.run(["cat", p])         # 3.6+ mein chalta hai (os.fspath protocol)
# some_old_api(p)                    # purane libraries fail kar sakti hain
some_old_api = str                    # demo
print(some_old_api(p))                # str() se convert karo

Gotcha 2 — glob order guaranteed nahi hai.

files = sorted(Path("tests").glob("test_*.py"))     # HAMESHA sort karo

Filesystem order OS aur filesystem par depend karta hai. Test reproducibility ke liye sort karna zaruri hai.

Gotcha 3 — resolve() vs absolute().

from pathlib import Path
p = Path("./tests/../src")
print(p.absolute())      # /current/dir/tests/../src   -- '..' waise ka waisa
print(p.resolve())       # /current/dir/src            -- normalise + symlinks resolve

Comparison ke liye hamesha resolve() use karo.

Gotcha 4 — mkdir bina parents=True.

# Path("a/b/c").mkdir()                    # FileNotFoundError agar 'a/b' nahi hai
Path("a/b/c").mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)     # sahi

Interview answer: "pathlib replaces string manipulation with path objects. The / operator makes composition readable, the components are properties — name, stem, suffix, parent — and the operations are methods on the object rather than a scattered set of functions, so autocomplete and type checking both work. It's also cross-platform: a Path becomes a WindowsPath or PosixPath automatically.

The patterns I actually use in a test framework: locating the project root from Path(__file__).resolve() walking up until I find pyproject.toml, rather than trusting the working directory, because that depends on where the command was invoked; sanitising pytest test IDs into filenames, since IDs contain brackets and colons that are illegal on Windows; and deque(f, maxlen=50) to keep the tail of a log with bounded memory. Two habits: always sort the result of glob, because filesystem order isn't guaranteed and reproducibility matters, and use resolve() rather than absolute() when comparing paths, because absolute leaves .. segments in place."

docs.title: Basics
docs.text:
import json
from pathlib import Path

data = {
    "run_id": "abc123",
    "total": 42,
    "pass_rate": 0.952,
    "passed": True,
    "error": None,
    "tests": [{"name": "test_login", "duration": 1.234}],
}

# --- Serialise (Python -> JSON) ---
text = json.dumps(data)                                  # compact string
pretty = json.dumps(data, indent=2, sort_keys=True)      # readable
Path("results.json").write_text(pretty, encoding="utf-8")

with open("results.json", "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
    json.dump(data, f, indent=2)                          # 'dump' -> file, 'dumps' -> string

# --- Deserialise (JSON -> Python) ---
loaded = json.loads(text)                                 # string se
loaded = json.loads(Path("results.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))

with open("results.json", encoding="utf-8") as f:
    loaded = json.load(f)                                 # file se

print(loaded == data)                                     # True

dump vs dumps yaad rakhne ka tareeka: s = string.

docs.title: Type mapping
docs.text:
Python JSON Wapas Python mein dict object dict list, tuple array list (tuple gayab!) str string str int number int float number float True / False true / false bool None null None set, datetime, Decimal, Path ERROR —

Round-trip mein data loss:

import json

original = {
    "tuple": (1, 2),
    "int_key": {1: "a"},
    "nan": float("nan"),
}

text = json.dumps(original)
back = json.loads(text)

print(back["tuple"])        # [1, 2]        <- tuple -> LIST
print(back["int_key"])      # {'1': 'a'}    <- int key -> STRING key
print(text)                 # {"nan": NaN}  <- NaN valid JSON NAHI hai!
print(original == back)     # False
  1. Tuple list ban jaata hai — JSON mein tuple ka concept nahi.
  2. Dict keys hamesha strings ban jaati hain — JSON object keys strings hi hoti hain. Ye sabse chupa hua bug hai: {1: "a"} round-trip ke baad {"1": "a"} hai, aur data[1] KeyError dega.
  3. NaN, Infinity — Python inhe likh deta hai par wo valid JSON nahi hai. Doosre parsers (JavaScript JSON.parse) reject karenge. allow_nan=False se error milega.

docs.title: Custom types serialise karna
docs.text:
import json
from dataclasses import dataclass, asdict, is_dataclass
from datetime import datetime, date
from decimal import Decimal
from pathlib import Path
from enum import Enum


class Status(str, Enum):
    PASSED = "passed"
    FAILED = "failed"


@dataclass
class TestResult:
    name: str
    status: Status
    duration: float
    started_at: datetime
    cost: Decimal
    artifact: Path


class QAEncoder(json.JSONEncoder):
    """Custom encoder for our domain types."""

    def default(self, obj):
        """Sirf tab call hota hai jab default serialisation FAIL ho."""
        if is_dataclass(obj) and not isinstance(obj, type):
            return asdict(obj)
        if isinstance(obj, (datetime, date)):
            return obj.isoformat()                     # '2026-08-23T14:05:23'
        if isinstance(obj, Decimal):
            return str(obj)                             # float NAHI -- precision bachao
        if isinstance(obj, Path):
            return str(obj)
        if isinstance(obj, set):
            return sorted(obj)                          # deterministic order
        if isinstance(obj, Enum):
            return obj.value
        return super().default(obj)                     # unknown -> TypeError


result = TestResult(
    name="test_checkout",
    status=Status.FAILED,
    duration=4.523,
    started_at=datetime(2026, 8, 23, 14, 5, 23),
    cost=Decimal("1299.99"),
    artifact=Path("artifacts/shot.png"),
)

print(json.dumps(result, cls=QAEncoder, indent=2))

Output:

{
  "name": "test_checkout",
  "status": "failed",
  "duration": 4.523,
  "started_at": "2026-08-23T14:05:23",
  "cost": "1299.99",
  "artifact": "artifacts/shot.png"
}

Line-by-line walkthrough:

  1. class QAEncoder(json.JSONEncoder): — default method sirf un objects par call hota hai jinhe json natively handle nahi kar sakta.
  2. is_dataclass(obj) and not isinstance(obj, type) — doosri condition zaruri hai kyunki is_dataclass class par bhi True deta hai, sirf instance par nahi.
  3. obj.isoformat() — ISO 8601. Ye sabse portable datetime format hai aur lexically sortable bhi hai. str(datetime) bhi similar hai par isoformat explicit hai.
  4. isinstance(obj, Decimal): return str(obj) — float(obj) mat karo! Decimal("1299.99") ko float banane se precision loss hoga. String se exact value preserve hoti hai, aur reader Decimal(value) se wapas bana sakta hai.
  5. sorted(obj) set ke liye — deterministic output. Bina sort ke, do runs mein alag order aayega aur diff bekaar ho jaayega.
  6. super().default(obj) — unknown types par parent ko do, jo TypeError raise karega. Ye line zaruri hai — bina iske default None return karega aur JSON mein null aayega, silently.

Simpler alternative — default function:

def json_default(obj):
    if isinstance(obj, datetime):
        return obj.isoformat()
    if isinstance(obj, Decimal):
        return str(obj)
    raise TypeError(f"Object of type {type(obj).__name__} is not JSON serializable")

print(json.dumps({"t": datetime.now()}, default=json_default))

Class banane ki zarurat nahi jab logic simple ho.

docs.title: Deserialising custom types
docs.text:
import json
from datetime import datetime


def json_object_hook(d: dict) -> dict:
    """Har JSON object par call hota hai -- strings ko types mein badlo."""
    for key, value in d.items():
        if isinstance(value, str) and key.endswith(("_at", "_time", "timestamp")):
            try:
                d[key] = datetime.fromisoformat(value)
            except ValueError:
                pass                                    # string hi rehne do
    return d


text = '{"name": "test_a", "started_at": "2026-08-23T14:05:23", "note": "hello"}'
parsed = json.loads(text, object_hook=json_object_hook)
print(type(parsed["started_at"]))     # <class 'datetime.datetime'>
print(type(parsed["note"]))           # <class 'str'>
  1. object_hook — har nested object par call hota hai, bottom-up.
  2. Naming convention par based conversion (_at suffix) — ye pragmatic hai par fragile. Schema se validate karna (pydantic) behtar hai.
  3. object_pairs_hook — pairs ki list deta hai, duplicate keys detect karne ke liye: 
    def detect_duplicates(pairs):
    seen = {}
    for k, v in pairs:
        if k in seen:
            raise ValueError(f"duplicate key: {k!r}")
        seen[k] = v
    return seen

# json.loads('{"a": 1, "a": 2}')                            # {'a': 2} -- silent!
# json.loads('{"a": 1, "a": 2}', object_pairs_hook=detect_duplicates)   # ValueError
    JSON spec duplicate keys ko undefined behaviour maanta hai, aur Python silently last wins karta hai. API response validation mein ye pakadna useful hai.

docs.title: Error handling
docs.text:
import json
from pathlib import Path


def load_json_safe(path: Path) -> dict:
    """JSON load karo, actionable errors ke saath."""
    try:
        text = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    except FileNotFoundError:
        raise FileNotFoundError(f"{path} not found. Did the test run produce output?") from None
    except UnicodeDecodeError as e:
        raise ValueError(f"{path} is not valid UTF-8 at byte {e.start}") from e

    try:
        return json.loads(text)
    except json.JSONDecodeError as e:
        # JSONDecodeError mein structured info hai
        lines = text.splitlines()
        context = lines[e.lineno - 1] if 0 < e.lineno <= len(lines) else "<unavailable>"
        pointer = " " * (e.colno - 1) + "^"
        raise ValueError(
            f"{path} is not valid JSON: {e.msg}\n"
            f"  line {e.lineno}, column {e.colno} (char {e.pos})\n"
            f"  {context}\n"
            f"  {pointer}"
        ) from e


# Example output:
# ValueError: results.json is not valid JSON: Expecting ',' delimiter
#   line 3, column 15 (char 42)
#   "total": 42 "passed": 40
#               ^

Line-by-line walkthrough:

  1. json.JSONDecodeError ke attributes: msg, doc (poora text), pos (character offset), lineno, colno. Ye structured hain — string parse karne ki zarurat nahi.
  2. lines[e.lineno - 1] — lineno 1-based hai, list 0-based.
  3. Pointer line (^) — ye error message ko turant actionable banata hai. Truncated JSON aur trailing comma ke liye ye bahut kaam ka hai.
  4. from None FileNotFoundError par — original noise hai (message already clear hai). from e JSONDecodeError par — original mein position info hai jo debugging mein kaam aa sakti hai.

docs.title: JSON Lines (JSONL) — streaming ke liye
docs.text:
import json
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Iterator


def write_jsonl(path: Path, records: Iterator[dict]) -> int:
    """Har record ek line par -- streaming-friendly."""
    count = 0
    with path.open("w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        for record in records:
            f.write(json.dumps(record, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n")
            count += 1
    return count


def read_jsonl(path: Path) -> Iterator[dict]:
    """Ek-ek record, constant memory."""
    with path.open(encoding="utf-8") as f:
        for line_no, line in enumerate(f, start=1):
            line = line.strip()
            if not line:
                continue
            try:
                yield json.loads(line)
            except json.JSONDecodeError as e:
                raise ValueError(f"{path}:{line_no}: {e.msg}") from e


results = [{"name": f"test_{i}", "status": "passed"} for i in range(1000)]
n = write_jsonl(Path("results.jsonl"), iter(results))
print(f"wrote {n} records")

failed = [r for r in read_jsonl(Path("results.jsonl")) if r["status"] == "failed"]
print(f"found {len(failed)} failures")

Kyun JSONL:

  1. Streaming — poori file memory mein nahi aati (Part 6).
  2. Appendable — running suite ke doraan results add kar sakte ho. Ek bade JSON array mein ye nahi ho sakta (closing ] chahiye).
  3. Crash-resistant — suite crash ho jaaye toh jitne records likhe gaye wo valid hain.
  4. Grep-able — grep '"status": "failed"' results.jsonl kaam karta hai.
  5. ensure_ascii=False — non-ASCII characters ko escape mat karo (é ki jagah é). File chhoti aur readable rehti hai. UTF-8 encoding zaruri hai tab.

import timeit

data = {"tests": [{"name": f"test_{i}", "duration": i * 0.1} for i in range(10_000)]}
text = json.dumps(data)

print(timeit.timeit(lambda: json.dumps(data), number=100))       # ~0.9s

  1. Stdlib json C-accelerated hai (_json module), toh already tez hai.
  2. orjson 3-10x tez hai aur datetime, UUID, dataclass natively handle karta hai. Bade report files ke liye consider karo.
  3. indent performance ko 2-3x slow karta hai — production output mein indent=None rakho, sirf human-readable files mein indent do.

docs.title: Gotchas
docs.text:
Gotcha 1 — dict keys strings ban jaati hain.

import json
d = {1: "a", 2: "b"}
back = json.loads(json.dumps(d))
print(back)                       # {'1': 'a', '2': 'b'}
# print(back[1])                  # KeyError: 1

Gotcha 2 — sort_keys=True deterministic output ke liye.

import json
a = {"z": 1, "a": 2}
b = {"a": 2, "z": 1}
print(json.dumps(a) == json.dumps(b))                      # False -- order alag
print(json.dumps(a, sort_keys=True) == json.dumps(b, sort_keys=True))    # True

Snapshot testing aur file diffing ke liye sort_keys=True zaruri hai.

Gotcha 3 — ensure_ascii default True hai.

import json
print(json.dumps({"city": "Bengalūru"}))                    # {"city": "Bengalūru"}
print(json.dumps({"city": "Bengalūru"}, ensure_ascii=False))# {"city": "Bengalūru"}

ensure_ascii=True safe hai (pure ASCII output) par bada aur unreadable. UTF-8 files ke liye False behtar hai.

Gotcha 4 — large integers.

import json
big = {"id": 2**63}
text = json.dumps(big)
print(text)                                                  # {"id": 9223372036854775808}
# JavaScript mein JSON.parse isko float bana dega -> PRECISION LOSS
# Fix: bade IDs ko STRING ki tarah bhejo

Interview answer: "json.dumps/loads for strings, dump/load for file objects. The mapping is lossy in ways that cause real bugs: tuples come back as lists, and every dict key becomes a string — so {1: 'a'} round-trips to {'1': 'a'} and the subsequent data[1] is a KeyError. Python will also happily write NaN and Infinity, which aren't valid JSON, so other parsers reject them. For domain types I pass a default function or a JSONEncoder subclass — datetimes as isoformat, Decimal as a string rather than a float so precision survives, sets as sorted lists so the output is deterministic — and I always call super().default() at the end, because otherwise unknown types silently become null.

On the reading side, JSONDecodeError carries lineno, colno, and pos, so I build an error message that shows the offending line with a caret under the column — that turns 'the config is broken' into a one-second fix. And for anything large I use JSON Lines rather than one big array: it streams with constant memory, it's appendable while a suite is still running, it survives a crash mid-run because every completed line is valid, and you can grep it."

line = 'test_login,"Failed: expected 200, got 500",4.5'

print(parts)
# ['test_login', '"Failed: expected 200', ' got 500"', '4.5']

import io

print(next(reader))

CSV format mein hain: quoting, escaped quotes, embedded newlines, alag delimiters, BOM. Manual parsing hamesha galat hoti hai.

docs.title: Reading
docs.text:
import csv
from pathlib import Path

# --- csv.reader: lists deta hai ---
with open("results.csv", newline="", encoding="utf-8") as f:
    reader = csv.reader(f)
    header = next(reader)                          # pehli row header hai
    print(header)                                   # ['name', 'status', 'duration']
    for row in reader:
        print(row[0], row[1])                       # index se access -- fragile

# --- csv.DictReader: dicts deta hai (PREFERRED) ---
with open("results.csv", newline="", encoding="utf-8") as f:
    reader = csv.DictReader(f)                      # pehli row automatically header
    print(reader.fieldnames)                        # ['name', 'status', 'duration']
    for row in reader:
        print(row["name"], row["status"])           # naam se access -- robust

# --- Custom fieldnames (file mein header nahi hai) ---
with open("no_header.csv", newline="", encoding="utf-8") as f:
    reader = csv.DictReader(f, fieldnames=["name", "status", "duration"])
    rows = list(reader)

# --- Alag delimiter (TSV) ---
with open("results.tsv", newline="", encoding="utf-8") as f:
    reader = csv.DictReader(f, delimiter="\t")
    rows = list(reader)

newline="" kyun MANDATORY hai:

# BINA newline="":
#   Text mode newline translation karta hai (\r\n -> \n).
#   CSV module apna newline handling karta hai (quoted fields mein embedded newlines).
#   Dono milkar CORRUPT karte hain:
#     - Windows par likhne mein: \r\r\n (double carriage return) -> extra blank rows
#     - Padhne mein: quoted fields ke andar ke newlines galat parse hote hain

# HAMESHA:
open("f.csv", newline="", encoding="utf-8")          # padhne aur likhne DONO mein

Ye Python docs mein explicitly likha hai aur ye sabse common CSV bug hai.

docs.title: Writing
docs.text:
import csv
from pathlib import Path

results = [
    {"name": "test_login", "status": "passed", "duration": 1.234, "error": ""},
    {"name": "test_cart", "status": "failed", "duration": 4.5,
     "error": 'Expected "Rs 1,299", got "Rs 0"'},
]

# --- DictWriter (preferred) ---
with open("results.csv", "w", newline="", encoding="utf-8") as f:
    writer = csv.DictWriter(
        f,
        fieldnames=["name", "status", "duration", "error"],
        extrasaction="raise",                       # extra keys par error (default)
        quoting=csv.QUOTE_MINIMAL,                  # sirf zarurat par quote
    )
    writer.writeheader()
    writer.writerows(results)

print(Path("results.csv").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))

Output:

name,status,duration,error
test_login,passed,1.234,
test_cart,failed,4.5,"Expected ""Rs 1,299"", got ""Rs 0"""

Line-by-line walkthrough:

  1. fieldnames=[...] — order define karta hai aur kaunsi keys likhni hain.
  2. extrasaction="raise" — agar dict mein extra key ho toh error. "ignore" se chupchaap skip hota hai. "raise" default hai aur behtar hai — silent data loss se bachaata hai.
  3. quoting=csv.QUOTE_MINIMAL — sirf tab quote karo jab zarurat ho (delimiter, quote, ya newline field mein ho). Options:
  4. QUOTE_ALL — sab quote karo
  5. QUOTE_NONNUMERIC — non-numeric quote karo, aur reading par numbers ko float banao
  6. QUOTE_NONE — kabhi quote mat karo (escapechar chahiye)
  7. Output mein ""Rs 1,299"" — embedded quotes doubled hote hain. Ye CSV standard (RFC 4180) hai. csv module ye automatically handle karta hai.
  8. writer.writeheader() — header row. Bhoolna common bug hai.

docs.title: Type conversion — CSV sab kuch string deta hai
docs.text:
import csv
from dataclasses import dataclass
from pathlib import Path


@dataclass
class TestResult:
    name: str
    status: str
    duration: float
    retries: int
    flaky: bool

    @classmethod
    def from_csv_row(cls, row: dict[str, str]) -> "TestResult":
        """CSV row (sab strings) se typed object."""
        return cls(
            name=row["name"].strip(),
            status=row["status"].strip().lower(),
            duration=float(row["duration"] or 0),               # khaali string -> 0
            retries=int(row["retries"] or 0),
            flaky=row["flaky"].strip().lower() in ("true", "1", "yes", "y"),
        )


def load_results(path: Path) -> list[TestResult]:
    results, errors = [], []
    with path.open(newline="", encoding="utf-8-sig") as f:      # BOM handle
        reader = csv.DictReader(f)
        for line_no, row in enumerate(reader, start=2):          # 2 = header ke baad pehli row
            try:
                results.append(TestResult.from_csv_row(row))
            except (ValueError, KeyError) as e:
                errors.append(f"line {line_no}: {type(e).__name__}: {e}")
    if errors:
        raise ValueError(f"{len(errors)} bad rows:\n  " + "\n  ".join(errors[:10]))
    return results

Line-by-line walkthrough:

  1. CSV mein sab strings hain — "4.5" string hai, float nahi. Conversion aapko karni padegi.
  2. float(row["duration"] or 0) — khaali string "" falsy hai, toh 0 use hoga. float("") ValueError deta hai.
  3. row["flaky"].strip().lower() in ("true", "1", "yes", "y") — bool("False") True hai! (1.6 gotcha). Explicit mapping zaruri hai.
  4. encoding="utf-8-sig" — Excel se export ki gayi CSV files mein BOM hota hai (\xef\xbb\xbf). utf-8 se padhoge toh pehla column ka naam "﻿name" ban jaayega aur row["name"] KeyError dega. utf-8-sig BOM ko automatically strip karta hai, aur BOM na ho toh bhi kaam karta hai. Ye sabse common CSV bug hai jab data Excel se aata hai.
  5. enumerate(reader, start=2) — line numbers error messages mein. start=2 kyunki line 1 header hai.
  6. errors[:10] — pehle 10 dikhao, warna 10,000 bad rows par error message unusable ho jaayega.

from typing import Iterator


def stream_csv(path: Path) -> Iterator[dict[str, str]]:

docs.title: Gotchas
docs.text:
Gotcha 1 — newline="" bhoolna. (upar detail mein)

Gotcha 2 — BOM.

# Excel se aayi file
# open("excel_export.csv", encoding="utf-8")       -> fieldnames[0] == '﻿name'
open("excel_export.csv", encoding="utf-8-sig")     # sahi

Gotcha 3 — Excel CSV ko interpret kar leta hai.

Aapne likha:  "007"      Excel dikhata hai:  7        (leading zeros gaye)
Aapne likha:  "1-2"      Excel dikhata hai:  02-Jan   (date bana diya)
Aapne likha:  "+91..."   Excel:              formula error
Aapne likha:  "=SUM(A1)" Excel:              FORMULA CHALA DI (CSV injection!)

CSV injection ek security issue hai — agar test data user input se aata hai aur report Excel mein khulti hai. Fix: =, +, -, @ se shuru hone wale fields ko ' se prefix karo.

Gotcha 4 — csv.writer writerow ko list chahiye, string nahi.

import csv, io
w = csv.writer(io.StringIO())
w.writerow("abc")                # ['a','b','c'] likh dega -- string iterate hui!
w.writerow(["abc"])              # sahi

Interview answer: "I always use the csv module rather than splitting on commas, because CSV has quoting, doubled quotes, embedded newlines, and multiple dialects — hand-rolled parsing breaks the first time an error message contains a comma. DictReader and DictWriter are the forms I use, so rows are accessed by column name and adding a column doesn't shift every index.

Two details that cause the bugs I've actually hit. First, newline='' is mandatory on both reading and writing — without it, the text layer's newline translation fights the csv module's own handling and you get blank rows on Windows and corrupted multi-line fields. Second, encoding='utf-8-sig' when the file might come from Excel, because Excel writes a BOM and with plain utf-8 your first column name becomes '﻿name', so row['name'] is a KeyError that only reproduces with files a human exported. Beyond that: every value is a string, so bool('False') is True and conversion has to be explicit; I do that in a from_csv_row classmethod on a dataclass and collect per-line errors with line numbers rather than failing on the first bad row."

docs.title: Kya hai
docs.text:
YAML "YAML Ain't Markup Language" — human-friendly config format. Python mein PyYAML (third-party) sabse common hai.

pip install pyyaml

docs.title: Basics
docs.text:
import yaml
from pathlib import Path

config_text = """
# Test framework configuration
environment: staging
base_url: https://staging.example.com

timeouts:
  default: 30000
  navigation: 60000
  assertion: 5000

browsers:
  - chromium
  - firefox
  - webkit

retry:
  attempts: 3
  delay: 0.5
  on_exceptions:
    - TimeoutError
    - ConnectionError

features:
  new_checkout: true
  legacy_login: false

credentials:
  username: test_user
  password: !!str 12345          # explicit string tag
"""

# --- Parse ---
config = yaml.safe_load(config_text)                    # SAFE_load, load NAHI
print(config["timeouts"]["default"])                    # 30000
print(config["browsers"])                                # ['chromium', 'firefox', 'webkit']
print(type(config["credentials"]["password"]))           # <class 'str'>

# --- Dump ---
print(yaml.safe_dump(config, sort_keys=False, default_flow_style=False, indent=2))

docs.title: safe_load vs load — SECURITY
docs.text:
import yaml

# --- DANGEROUS ---
malicious = """
!!python/object/apply:os.system
args: ['rm -rf /tmp/important']
"""
# yaml.load(malicious, Loader=yaml.Loader)      # ARBITRARY CODE EXECUTION!

# --- SAFE ---
# yaml.safe_load(malicious)
# yaml.constructor.ConstructorError: could not determine a constructor
#     for the tag 'tag:yaml.org,2002:python/object/apply:os.system'

Rules:

  1. Hamesha yaml.safe_load use karo, yaml.load nahi.
  2. PyYAML 5.1+ mein yaml.load bina Loader argument ke warning deta hai; 6.0 mein Loader mandatory hai.
  3. yaml.safe_dump bhi use karo (yaml.dump Python-specific tags likh sakta hai).
  4. Ye ek real CVE class hai — CI configs jo untrusted sources se aate hain, unpar yaml.load remote code execution deta hai.

sweden           SE           str
yes_value        True         bool
no_value         False        bool
on_value         True         bool
off_value        False        bool
true_value       True         bool
version          1.0          float         <- "1.0" -> float, "1" nahi
version_str      1.0          str
version_multi    1.0.0        str           <- teen dots -> string
octal_looking    755          int           <- YAML 1.1 mein 0755 octal tha; PyYAML 493 de sakta hai
sha_prefix       31           int           <- 0x1F hex -> 31
time_like        750          int           <- 12:30 sexagesimal -> 12*60+30 = 750 !!!
big_num          1000000      int
null_1           None         NoneType
null_2           None         NoneType
null_3           None         NoneType
empty_str                     str

Line-by-line walkthrough — ye sab REAL bugs hain:

  1. The Norway Problem: NO → False. Country codes ki list mein Norway boolean ban jaata hai. Ye YAML 1.1 spec ka famous issue hai. yes, no, on, off, y, n — sab booleans hain.
  2. version: 1.0 → float 1.0. Agar aap "1.0" string expect kar rahe the toh config["version"].split(".") AttributeError dega.
  3. version_multi: 1.0.0 → string (kyunki wo valid number nahi).
  4. time_like: 12:30 → 750. YAML 1.1 mein a:b sexagesimal (base-60) number hai: 12*60 + 30 = 750. Ye time values ko silently corrupt karta hai.
  5. sha_prefix: 0x1F → 31. Git SHAs jo 0x se shuru ho... integer ban jaate hain.
  6. null_3: (khaali value) → None. Ye aksar unintended hota hai.

Fix — hamesha quote karo:

# SAHI
country: "NO"
version: "1.0"
time: "12:30"
sha: "0x1F"
enabled: true          # actual boolean -- quote MAT karo
timeout: 30000         # actual number -- quote mat karo

Rule: agar value ek string honi chahiye, use quote karo. Hamesha.

docs.title: Validation — YAML sirf parse karta hai, validate nahi
docs.text:
import yaml
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from pathlib import Path


@dataclass
class RetryConfig:
    attempts: int = 3
    delay: float = 0.5

    def __post_init__(self):
        if not isinstance(self.attempts, int) or self.attempts < 1:
            raise ValueError(f"retry.attempts must be a positive int, got {self.attempts!r}")
        if not isinstance(self.delay, (int, float)) or self.delay < 0:
            raise ValueError(f"retry.delay must be a non-negative number, got {self.delay!r}")


@dataclass
class TestConfig:
    environment: str
    base_url: str
    browsers: list[str] = field(default_factory=lambda: ["chromium"])
    timeout: int = 30_000
    retry: RetryConfig = field(default_factory=RetryConfig)

    VALID_BROWSERS = frozenset({"chromium", "firefox", "webkit"})
    VALID_ENVS = frozenset({"local", "dev", "staging", "prod"})

    def __post_init__(self):
        if self.environment not in self.VALID_ENVS:
            raise ValueError(
                f"environment must be one of {sorted(self.VALID_ENVS)}, got {self.environment!r}"
            )
        if not self.base_url.startswith(("http://", "https://")):
            raise ValueError(f"base_url must be absolute, got {self.base_url!r}")
        bad = set(self.browsers) - self.VALID_BROWSERS
        if bad:
            raise ValueError(f"unknown browsers: {sorted(bad)}")
        if isinstance(self.retry, dict):                       # YAML se dict aayi hai
            self.retry = RetryConfig(**self.retry)

    @classmethod
    def from_yaml(cls, path: Path) -> "TestConfig":
        try:
            raw = yaml.safe_load(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        except yaml.YAMLError as e:
            mark = getattr(e, "problem_mark", None)
            location = f" at line {mark.line + 1}, column {mark.column + 1}" if mark else ""
            raise ValueError(f"{path} is not valid YAML{location}: {e}") from e

        if raw is None:
            raise ValueError(f"{path} is empty")
        if not isinstance(raw, dict):
            raise ValueError(f"{path} must contain a mapping, got {type(raw).__name__}")

        known = {f for f in cls.__dataclass_fields__}
        unknown = set(raw) - known
        if unknown:
            raise ValueError(
                f"{path}: unknown keys {sorted(unknown)}; valid keys are {sorted(known)}"
            )
        return cls(**raw)

Line-by-line walkthrough:

  1. yaml.safe_load — hamesha.
  2. e.problem_mark — PyYAML ke error mein line/column info hai. mark.line 0-based hai, isliye +1.
  3. if raw is None: raise — khaali YAML file None deti hai, khaali dict nahi. Ye cls(**None) par TypeError deta jo confusing hota.
  4. if not isinstance(raw, dict) — top-level ek list ya string bhi ho sakti hai. Explicit check better error deta hai.
  5. unknown = set(raw) - known — typo detection. timout: 5000 (typo) chupchaap ignore hone ki jagah error dega. Ye config bugs ka sabse bada source hai.
  6. if isinstance(self.retry, dict): self.retry = RetryConfig(**self.retry) — nested dict ko nested dataclass mein badla. Dataclass ye automatically nahi karta.
  7. __post_init__ mein validation — 5.8.

Behtar: pydantic use karo

# pip install pydantic
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field, HttpUrl, field_validator
from typing import Literal


class RetryConfig(BaseModel):
    attempts: int = Field(default=3, ge=1, le=10)
    delay: float = Field(default=0.5, ge=0)


class TestConfig(BaseModel):
    model_config = {"extra": "forbid"}                  # unknown keys -> error

    environment: Literal["local", "dev", "staging", "prod"]
    base_url: HttpUrl
    browsers: list[Literal["chromium", "firefox", "webkit"]] = ["chromium"]
    timeout: int = Field(default=30_000, gt=0)
    retry: RetryConfig = RetryConfig()

    @field_validator("browsers")
    @classmethod
    def no_duplicates(cls, v: list[str]) -> list[str]:
        if len(v) != len(set(v)):
            raise ValueError("duplicate browsers")
        return v


# config = TestConfig.model_validate(yaml.safe_load(path.read_text()))
  1. Literal[...] — allowed values type mein. Validation automatic.
  2. Field(ge=1, le=10) — constraints declaratively.
  3. extra: "forbid" — unknown keys error dete hain.
  4. HttpUrl — URL validation built-in.
  5. Pydantic ka error message bahut achha hota hai — har field ka path aur problem batata hai.
  6. 20 lines ka manual validation 8 lines ka schema ban gaya, aur error messages behtar hain.
